docs.title: 7. What gets assessed
docs.text:
Component Weight Evidence Lab completion (7 labs) 30% checkpoint notebooks + expected outputs PA-1 (Day 2) + PA-2 (Day 3) 20% corrected analyses + written diagnoses Quiz (10 of the 20 questions, 15 min, closed book) 10% instructor/QUIZ_BANK.md Capstone 40% frozen plan, analysis, memo — reasoning first

Pass ≥ 70. Distinction ≥ 90. The Causal badge requires ≥ 70 overall and capstone ≥ 70 and zero academic-integrity flags. A correct, well-justified null or non-identifiability verdict never counts against a participant.

docs.title: 8. Vocabulary used consistently throughout
docs.text:
Term Meaning as used here OEC Overall Evaluation Criterion — the single primary decision metric. Exactly one per experiment. Guardrail A metric that must not get worse, tested as a family with FWER control. Trigger Whether a unit actually reached the changed step. The analysis population is triggered users, not all assigned users. Estimand The causal quantity you are after (ATE / ATT / LATE / CATE), named before touching data. Frozen plan The design doc + analysis plan, hashed and committed before results exist. causal_utils.freeze_plan() stamps and hashes it. Practical threshold The effect size below which the result does not justify acting. Distinct from statistical significance.

All code targets Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended). Every causal method is taught simulation-first on the Injaz golden thread: plant a known effect, recover it, then apply it where the truth is unknown.

docs.title: Capstone Brief — The Injaz Experimentation and Impact Evaluation Package
docs.text: SDA-DSC-213 · Experimentation, A/B Testing and Causal Inference · SDAIA Academy Participant-facing brief · Day 4 · 40% of the course grade

docs.title: 1. Scenario
docs.text:
You are the experimentation lead assigned to Injaz (إنجاز), the unified Saudi digital-government services platform where citizens renew licences, issue certificates, update addresses and pay fees online.

Leadership faces two linked decisions before the next budget cycle.

Decision 1 — the AI-assisted autofill feature. A new AI-assisted document-and-form autofill feature has been running as a randomised A/B test. It is intended to raise the service-completion rate. Leadership wants to know whether to launch it nationally. The build-and-run cost is real, so the programme board has set a practical-significance threshold of +1.0 percentage point on completion: an effect smaller than that does not pay for the feature, however clean the p-value. Data: injaz_autofill_ab.csv (+ injaz_pre_period.csv for CUPED).

Decision 2 — the regional reminder-notification programme. Last year a reminder-notification programme was rolled out region by region, in waves, without randomisation. Leadership wants to know whether to scale it nationally. There was never a control arm; there is a panel of regions over 24 months and four activation waves, with four regions never activated. Data: injaz_regions_panel.csv (and injaz_regions_panel_pretrend.csv, injaz_users.csv if you use them).

The two decisions are linked because they compete for the same budget and will be presented on the same slide. Your mandate: design and analyse a clean experiment for the feature, produce a credible causal evaluation of the pilot where randomisation was impossible, and deliver a decision memo leadership can act on.

Everything you built in Labs 1–7 is a component. The capstone is the integration, plus your own rigour and communication.

docs.title: 2. Mandatory requirements
docs.text:
These map one-to-one onto the grading rubric in §6.

# Requirement Maps to 1 Design. A frozen design doc for the autofill A/B test: randomisation unit + justification, the OEC, ≥ 3 guardrails, the trigger definition, the unit of analysis, and a written analysis plan produced before analysis. LO1 2 Power. A sizing analysis: required per-arm sample and run-length plan for your chosen MDE, including the arm multiplier and the trigger rate, plus a CUPED-adjusted alternative with its quantified saving. LO2 3 Experiment integrity. Deterministic hash assignment, a passing SRM check, and a covariate-balance table (all SMD < 0.1). An experiment that fails these must be reported as invalid, not analysed anyway. LO1 / LO3 4 Analysis. The autofill effect with correct (robust or clustered) variance, a CUPED adjustment, guardrails checked with the correct multiple-testing family, and a clear statistical-vs-practical-significance verdict against the design threshold. LO3 5 Causal evaluation. A quasi-experimental evaluation of the reminder pilot — DiD with an event-study parallel-trends check, or matching with a sensitivity analysis — including the DAG / identifying assumption and ≥ 2 refutation or validation checks. LO4 / LO5 6 Communication. A one-page decision memo: effect sizes and confidence intervals in business units, a ship / scale / hold recommendation per intervention, the key assumptions stated as risks, and an explicit "what would change this." LO6 7 Reproducibility & rigour. A clean, runnable notebook or repo; a fixed random seed; the frozen analysis plan versioned before results; no peeking-driven stopping; honest treatment of any null or non-identifiable result. LO3

docs.title: Choose at least one extension
docs.text:
Extension What it must show Heterogeneous treatment effects (CATE) on the autofill test with EconML (causal forest) the subgroup structure, and an honest note on multiple testing across subgroups Always-valid / sequential inference on the autofill test a confidence sequence that would have made continuous monitoring legitimate, contrasted with the fixed-horizon interval Staggered-DiD estimator (Callaway–Sant'Anna or Sun–Abraham) on the full multi-wave reminder rollout the cohort-aware estimate compared against naive TWFE, and why they differ Instrumental-variables estimate of the effect of filing channel on completion a defended instrument (all three conditions argued) and the first-stage F Power / variance-reduction study how much CUPED and stratification would shorten future Injaz experiments, in days

Extensions add up to +5 bonus, capped at 100, and only if your mandatory scope is already ≥ 80. A shaky extension bolted onto a weak core scores nothing.

docs.title: 3. Target architecture
docs.text:
Frame ──> Design doc (frozen plan) ──> Power/sizing ──> [A/B: assign → SRM → balance → analyse]
                                                     └─> [Pilot: DAG → identify → estimate → refute]
   A/B effect (CUPED, robust CI) ─┐
   Pilot effect (DiD/matching CI) ┼──> reconcile ──> Decision plot (vs threshold) ──> Decision memo
   guardrails + validation ───────┘                                                    (ship/scale/hold)
Reproducible notebook: fixed seed · frozen plan versioned before results · honest nulls

causal_utils gives you every piece of this. You are not being graded on re-implementing did_twfe; you are being graded on whether you used it on the right rows, with the right standard errors, and said the right thing about it.

docs.title: 4. Deliverables
docs.text:
1. A runnable analysis notebook (or repo) covering design, power, A/B analysis and causal evaluation, with a fixed seed and a clean top-to-bottom run. Start from notebooks/capstone_starter.ipynb.
  2. The frozen design doc + analysis plan — timestamped and hashed before the results section. Use capstone/DESIGN_DOC_TEMPLATE.md and causal_utils.freeze_plan(); put the plan hash in the memo.
  3. Experiment-integrity evidence — the SRM result and the covariate-balance table, printed in the notebook.
  4. A causal-evaluation section — DAG, identifying assumption, estimate with CI, and refutation/validation output.
  5. A one-page decision memo — the decision plot, per-intervention recommendations, quantified uncertainty, and "what would change this." Use capstone/DECISION_MEMO_TEMPLATE.md.
  6. A 6-minute presentation — the two decisions, the evidence and its limits, and the recommendation.

Submit the notebook, the frozen design doc and the memo. Run capstone/SELF_AUDIT_CHECKLIST.md before you submit; every item is answerable yes or no.

docs.title: 5. Milestones
docs.text:
Day 4 clock times. The gate must be met to move on — an instructor will spot-check.

Milestone Due Time Gate M-A framed question + frozen design doc + sizing Day 4 H3 start · 11:00 instructor spot-check of the plan — the plan is hashed before any results cell has been run M-B A/B analysed: SRM, balance, effect, guardrails Day 4 H3 end · 11:50 integrity checks pass (or the experiment is declared invalid, with evidence) M-C pilot evaluated: DiD or matching + validation Day 4 H4 mid · 13:05 a refutation or validation check is present and its result is stated M-D decision memo + extension complete Day 4 H4 end · 13:30 full self-audit checklist completed M-E presentation + submission Day 4 H5 · 13:40–14:30 rubric scoring, live

If you are behind at M-A, cut the extension, not the freeze. A plan frozen after results is worth zero on criterion 1 and caps criterion 7.

docs.title: 6. Grading rubric (100 points)
docs.text:
Criterion Weight 90–100% band 70–89% band < 70% band Experiment design & analysis plan 15 Unit justified, OEC + guardrails sound, plan frozen before results Minor gaps (thin guardrails, late freeze) No plan / metrics chosen after seeing data Power & sample sizing 15 Correct sizing incl. arms, trigger, floor; CUPED saving quantified Mostly correct; one factor omitted Wrong or missing sizing; under-run unrecognised Experiment integrity 10 SRM + balance correct; invalid experiments flagged Checks present but partial No SRM/balance; invalid test analysed anyway A/B analysis correctness 20 Robust/clustered variance, CUPED, correct correction family, practical-vs-statistical verdict 1–2 issues (naive SE or missing correction) Naive t-test, no correction, p-value worship Causal evaluation 20 DAG + assumption stated; DiD/matching valid; ≥ 2 refutations; sensitivity honest Method sound; validation thin No identification argument; unvalidated claim Decision communication 15 One-page memo: effects + CIs in business units, clear recommendation, risks + "what would change this" Memo works; uncertainty understated p-values to leadership; overstated certainty Reproducibility & integrity 5 Clean seeded run; honest nulls; no peeking Minor reproducibility gaps Non-runnable; peeking-driven stop

Pass ≥ 70. Distinction ≥ 90.

docs.title: Anti-patterns that cap a criterion at 70%
docs.text:
• Metrics chosen after seeing the data.
  • Peeking-driven stopping.
  • Controlling for a mediator or a collider.
  • Presenting an observational estimate with no identifying assumption and no refutation.
  • Reporting bare p-values to leadership.

docs.title: One thing you will be asked live
docs.text: During your briefing you will be asked to state, out loud: the identifying assumption behind your causal estimate, and the single unmeasured variable that would break it. Prepare that sentence.

docs.title: 7. "We cannot conclude" is a full-marks answer
docs.text:
Read this twice.

A correct, well-argued "we cannot conclude" earns full marks on the criteria it touches. A defensible hold, keep running or not identifiable — here is what would be needed is a top-band answer. This is not a consolation prize and it is not grading on a curve: it is the graded skill.

What makes it full marks rather than a shrug is that all four of these are present:

  1. The number and its uncertainty, stated in business units — not "no effect", but "+X.X pp, 95% CI [a, b]".
  2. What that interval rules out and what it does not. An interval that excludes zero but straddles the decision threshold means "real, but we cannot show it is big enough to pay for" — a completely different sentence from "no effect".
  3. Why it is not conclusive — under-powered for the threshold, an assumption that fails its check, an estimand that is not the one leadership asked about.
  4. What would change it — a specific, costed next step: run N more days, measure variable V, find a wave with a clean never-treated comparison.

What is not full marks: "the p-value was 0.06 so nothing happened", or a verdict of ship justified by significance alone when the confidence interval crosses the decision threshold.

docs.title: 8. What excellent looks like
docs.text:
The distinction band is not about more code. It is about six habits.

1. The estimand is named before the data is touched. Excellent: "The ATT of autofill exposure on service completion among triggered users, over the 21-day run." Weak: "the effect of autofill." If your memo says "the effect" without saying on whom, over what window, you have not answered the question that was asked.

2. The analysis population is the triggered population, and you say so. The trigger is not a technicality. Assigned users who never reached the changed step cannot have been affected by it, so including them dilutes the estimate toward zero by roughly the trigger rate. Excellent work states the trigger definition in the frozen plan, filters on it, reports the trigger rate, and — if it also reports the all-assigned number — labels it correctly as the intention-to-treat estimate for a different question.

3. The confidence interval is compared to the decision threshold, not to zero. Zero is not the decision boundary; the programme board's +1.0 pp is. Excellent work draws the decision plot with the threshold line on it and reads it out: "the point estimate clears the bar, the interval does not." Statistical significance answers is it there; practical significance answers is it worth it. Both sentences appear in a top-band memo.

4. Assumptions are named, checked where checkable, and priced where not. Parallel trends is not "assumed" — it is supported by flat pre-period event-study coefficients, or it is not, and you say which. Unconfoundedness in a matching design is never checkable; excellent work replaces "we assume unconfoundedness" with "a hidden confounder that changed the odds of enrolling by more than Γ ≈ x would overturn this." Naming the specific unmeasured variable that would break your estimate — and admitting you cannot rule it out — reads as confidence, not weakness.

5. Disagreements are reconciled, not cherry-picked. When the experimental and observational estimates point different ways, or when TWFE disagrees with a cohort-aware estimator, an excellent answer explains the gap through the assumption most likely to be violated (staggered timing, ramp-in, a different estimand, a different population) and reports both numbers. A memo that quietly keeps the convenient one is an integrity flag.

6. The memo would survive a hostile board member. One page. Effects and intervals in percentage points of completion, translated into completions per month where it helps. A recommendation per intervention, stated in the first three lines. Risks as risks. One sentence of "what would change this." No p-values, no jargon, no hedging that hides the recommendation.

Two more things that separate top-band work in practice: the notebook runs top-to-bottom on a clean kernel with a fixed seed, and the plan hash in the memo matches the plan hash in the notebook. Both take two minutes and both are checked.

docs.title: 9. Bonus tasks (early finishers / distinction seekers)
docs.text:
1. Reproduce the peeking hazard on your own A/B data, then contrast a sequential method that would have been valid.
  2. Add a Rosenbaum-bounds sensitivity analysis quantifying how strong hidden bias must be to overturn the pilot conclusion.
  3. Package your causal_utils work as a documented mini-package (assignment, SRM, balance, sizing, DiD, refutation).
  4. Produce a second decision plot showing how the recommendation changes under the most pessimistic credible assumptions.

docs.title: 10. Academic integrity
docs.text: Identical simulated seeds and identical results across submissions are checked. Work in your own notebook. Reuse causal_utils and your own Lab 1–7 code freely — that is the point of building it. The Causal badge requires ≥ 70 overall, capstone ≥ 70, and zero integrity flags.

docs.title: Decision Memo — template and worked example
docs.text:
SDA-DSC-213 Capstone · Injaz (إنجاز) · SDAIA Academy

The memo is one page. Not one page of 8-point type — one page a board member reads in three minutes and can act on. It is worth 15 of 100 points, and it is the artefact SDA-DSC-311 consumes as an input.

Three rules, and they are the ones that get marked:

  1. Effects and confidence intervals in business units. Percentage points of completion, and where it helps, completions per month. No p-values. No "statistically significant" as a synonym for "true".
  2. A recommendation per intervention, in the first five lines. Ship, scale, hold-and-extend, or stop. Leadership should not have to hunt for it.
  3. Assumptions stated as risks, plus one explicit "what would change this." A specific, costed next step — not "further research is needed."

docs.title: Part A — The skeleton
docs.text: Copy everything between the rules. Keep the headings; they are what the rubric is read against.

docs.title: MEMO
docs.text:
To: decision-maker / board From: your name, experimentation lead Date: date Subject: the two decisions, in one line Analysis plan hash: plan_hash from freeze_plan() — frozen before results

Recommendation

  • [Intervention 1]: [SHIP / SCALE / HOLD AND EXTEND / STOP]. One clause of why.
  • [Intervention 2]: [SHIP / SCALE / HOLD AND EXTEND / STOP]. One clause of why.

What we found

Intervention Effect on completion 95% CI In business units Decision threshold Verdict

Two or three sentences of plain-language reading. What the interval rules out and what it does not.

Guardrails

One line per guardrail family: did anything get worse, and by how much, after the correct multiple-testing correction.

How much to believe it

Intervention Design Identifying assumption Evidence it holds What would break it

Risks

  1. Risk stated as a risk, with its consequence. 2. 3.

What would change this

One sentence. A specific, costed action and what it would tell you.

Decision plot

Insert decision_plot(...) — effects with intervals, and the threshold line.

docs.title: Part B — Worked example
docs.text: This is the standard. It is the autofill decision from the capstone data, written to length, with the real numbers a correct analysis produces. Your memo will have different wording and must cover both interventions; the point here is the shape, the register, and the honesty.

docs.title: MEMO
docs.text:
To: Injaz Programme Board From: Experimentation Lead, Injaz Analytics Date: Day 4 of the cohort Subject: AI autofill — national launch decision; regional reminders — scale decision Analysis plan hash: b47e305fe7c0… (frozen before any result was computed)

Recommendation

  • AI autofill: HOLD AND EXTEND — do not launch nationally yet. The feature works, but the evidence cannot yet show it is large enough to pay for. One more week of the current test would settle it.
  • Regional reminders: SCALE to the four regions that never activated. The effect is well above the bar and survives every check we can run on it.

What we found

Intervention Effect on completion 95% CI In business units Threshold Verdict AI autofill (A/B, CUPED-adjusted, n = 49,510 triggered users) +1.6 pp +0.8 to +2.4 pp ≈ +4,400 completions/month, but plausibly as few as +2,100 or as many as +6,600 +1.0 pp Real, but not shown to clear the bar Regional reminders (difference-in-differences, 13 regions × 24 months) +2.6 pp +2.5 to +2.7 pp ≈ +100 completions/month in the four never-activated regions +1.0 pp Clears the bar

Autofill raised service completion by 1.6 percentage points, from 55.1% to 56.6% among users who actually reached the autofill step. That effect is real: the interval does not include zero. It is not, however, the question the board asked. The board's bar is +1.0 pp, and the interval runs from +0.8 to +2.4 pp — it straddles the bar. The most likely value is comfortably above the threshold; a value below it has not been ruled out. Launching nationally today means accepting a genuine chance that the feature does not repay its build and run cost.

The reminder programme is a different picture. It was never randomised, so the estimate rests on an assumption rather than on a design — but the assumption is supported, the interval is narrow, and it sits entirely above the bar.

Guardrails

Four guardrails were pre-registered and tested as one family with a Bonferroni correction (m = 4). None regressed. Support-contact rate rose 0.2 pp (−0.2 to +0.5 pp before correction; not significant after it) — the only metric worth watching in a longer run. Upload errors were flat (−0.3 pp, indistinguishable from zero). Two guardrails moved in our favour and survived the correction: time-to-complete fell about 10 seconds per session, and drop-off fell 1.3 pp.

How much to believe it

Intervention Design Identifying assumption Evidence it holds What would break it Autofill Randomised A/B, user-level hash assignment Randomisation — no assumption beyond the mechanics working Sample-ratio check passes (35,016 vs 34,984; p = 0.90); all 21 covariate cells balanced, worst |SMD| = 0.019 A logging bug that drops treated users non-randomly; the SRM check is our detector and it is clean Reminders Difference-in-differences, region-clustered errors Parallel trends — absent the programme, activated and never-activated regions would have moved together Event study: the five estimated pre-activation coefficients (relative months −6 to −2, baseline −1) all sit within ±0.5 pp of zero and none is distinguishable from zero A region-specific initiative launched at the same time as activation; we cannot rule this out from the data

Risks

  1. The autofill estimate is precise enough to detect the effect, not precise enough to price it. Acting on the point estimate alone treats an outcome the data still permits — a true effect below +1.0 pp — as though it had been ruled out.
  2. The reminder effect is observational. Regions chose their activation order. Parallel trends is supported in the pre-period but is untestable for the post-period, and one unmeasured region-level initiative would overturn it.
  3. The reminder number is probably an underestimate. The programme ramps in over roughly two months, and the standard two-way fixed-effects estimator averages the weak early months in with the mature ones. A cohort-aware estimator puts the mature effect nearer +3.3 pp. This risk points in the safe direction for a scale decision.
  4. Support contacts. The one guardrail that moved against us did so modestly and did not survive correction, but a national launch multiplies the volume; it should be a stop-condition in the extended run.

What would change this

Run the autofill test for one more week — about 50,000 more triggered users, which the platform supplies in roughly 7 running days. That would narrow the interval by a factor of about 1.4 and is enough to place the whole interval on one side of the +1.0 pp bar. If the lower bound then clears +1.0 pp, launch; if the interval settles below it, the feature is real and not worth the build, and we stop.

docs.title: Part C — How the example scores, line by line
docs.text:
Read this next to the rubric row for Decision communication (15 points).

What the example does Why it earns the mark Recommendation in the first five lines, one per intervention, with a verb (HOLD AND EXTEND, SCALE) The board can stop reading after five lines and still act "+1.6 pp, 95% CI +0.8 to +2.4 pp" and "≈ +4,400 completions/month, plausibly as few as +2,100" Effect and interval, in business units. The interval is translated too — this is where most memos quietly drop the uncertainty "The interval straddles the bar" The practical-vs-statistical distinction made in one sentence a non-statistician understands No p-values anywhere in the body The one p-value that appears (SRM, p = 0.90) is a validity check, not a finding Guardrails reported as a family, with the correction named Criterion 4 wants the correct correction family, and criterion 6 wants it stated plainly A table of assumptions with "what would break it" Assumptions as risks, not as boilerplate. The right-hand column is the sentence you will be asked for live Risk 3 says the estimate is probably too low Honest uncertainty runs in both directions. A memo whose caveats all conveniently point one way reads as advocacy "One more week — about 50,000 more triggered users, roughly 7 running days" "What would change this" is specific and costed. "More data is needed" earns nothing The plan hash in the header Criterion 7 evidence, at the cost of one line

Length check. Part B is one page at 11 pt. If yours is longer, the first things to cut are: method names, the word "statistically", and any sentence that explains what a confidence interval is.

docs.title: Part D — Phrases to use, and phrases that cost you marks
docs.text: Instead of Write "The result was statistically significant (p < 0.05), so we recommend shipping." "The effect is +1.6 pp (95% CI +0.8 to +2.4). Our bar is +1.0 pp, and the interval straddles it — so we cannot yet say it is big enough to pay for." "There was no effect." "We could not distinguish the effect from zero at this sample size; effects up to +X pp remain consistent with what we saw." "We assume parallel trends." "The comparison assumes activated and never-activated regions would have moved together. The five estimated pre-activation coefficients sit within ±0.5 pp of zero, which supports it; a region-specific initiative timed with activation would break it." "Further research is needed." "One more week — 50,000 more triggered users, about 7 running days — would place the whole interval on one side of the bar." "The model controls for support calls, distance and device age." (delete — and check that support calls is not a mediator you have just controlled away) "The lift was 1.6%." "The completion rate rose 1.6 percentage points, from 55.1% to 56.6%." Percent and percentage points are different numbers and reviewers check.

docs.title: Design Doc & Analysis Plan — FROZEN
docs.text:
SDA-DSC-213 Capstone · Injaz (إنجاز) · SDAIA Academy

Fill this in before you look at a single outcome. Every field below is a commitment. Once it is frozen and hashed, changing it means saying so in the memo — not quietly editing.

The fields map one-to-one onto causal_utils.AnalysisPlan. When the document is complete, build the object, call freeze_plan(), and paste the printed timestamp and hash into §9 of this document. freeze_plan() must run before any cell that computes an outcome.

docs.title: 0. Header
docs.text: Field Value Participant your name Cohort / date experiment_name slug, e.g. injaz-autofill-2026q4 Version 1.0 Status DRAFT → FROZEN (change this line when you freeze)

docs.title: 1. The decision
docs.text:
decision — What decision does this experiment inform, and who makes it? One sentence, in the decision-maker's words. "Launch AI autofill nationally, or not?" — not "test whether autofill works."

Why now / what happens if we get it wrong? One or two sentences on the cost of a wrong ship and the cost of a wrong hold. This is what sets your threshold in §5.

docs.title: 2. The causal question
docs.text:
Estimand — the causal quantity, named precisely. ATE / ATT / LATE / CATE, on which outcome, for which population, over which window. "The ATT of autofill exposure on service completion among triggered users over the 21-day run."

Potential-outcomes statement. Write it as a contrast: Y(1) − Y(0) where Y(1) = _ and Y(0) = _ .

Why is this estimand the one leadership needs? One sentence. If you would report ATT but they will roll out to everyone, say so and say why it is still the right number.

docs.title: 3. Design
docs.text:
randomisation_unit — What is randomised? user / session / region / device. Name the field the hash is computed on.

Justification of the unit (two sentences). Why this unit and not the finer one. Consistency of experience across returning visits, interference, and what the coarser unit costs you in power.

Assignment mechanism. Deterministic hash + salt. Give the exact salt string. Same id must always map to the same arm, across sessions and across reruns.

Arms and allocation. e.g. 2 arms, 50/50. If unequal, say why and note the power cost.

SUTVA / interference audit — two plausible violations and the design change each would require.

# Plausible violation Design change it would require 1 2

Eligibility / exclusions. Who is in the pool, who is filtered out, and — critically — is the filter measured before assignment? A post-assignment filter breaks randomisation.

docs.title: 4. Metrics
docs.text:
oec — the Overall Evaluation Criterion. Exactly one. The single metric the decision turns on, with its exact definition (numerator, denominator, window).

trigger_definition — what counts as having reached the changed step? Be operational: "the user reached the document-upload step at least once during the run." This defines your analysis population.

unit_of_analysis — the row in the final analysis table. Must be the randomisation unit, or you must cluster. State which.

guardrails — at least three metrics that must not get worse.

# Guardrail metric Direction that would alarm you Tolerance / what "worse" means 1 2 3 4

Metrics explicitly NOT being used as the OEC. Naming what you are not going to promote to primary later is half of what a freeze buys you.

docs.title: 5. Decision rule
docs.text:
practical_threshold — the effect size below which you would not act. In business units, with its justification (build cost, run cost, opportunity cost). Not a statistical quantity.

mde — the minimum detectable effect you are powering for. State the relationship to the threshold: powering for an MDE larger than your threshold means a "non-significant" result cannot rule out an actionable effect.

alpha / power. Defaults are 0.05 and 0.80. If you changed either, justify it here.

The decision rule, written as an if-statement before the data exists. "Ship if the 95% CI lies entirely above +1.0 pp and no guardrail regresses past its tolerance. Hold and extend if the point estimate clears the threshold but the interval straddles it. Stop if ____ ."

docs.title: 6. Sizing and run length
docs.text:
Quantity Value Note Baseline rate on the OEC from pre-period, not from the running experiment MDE (absolute) planned_n_per_arm Number of arms the arm multiplier applies to traffic, not to n per arm Trigger rate fraction of eligible users who reach the changed step Daily eligible traffic Daily usable (eligible × trigger) planned_run_days rounded up to whole weeks — weekday and weekend users are different people CUPED covariate must be pre-treatment Expected variance reduction CUPED-adjusted n per arm CUPED-adjusted run days the saving, in days, is the number to quote

Sizing paragraph for the design doc (one paragraph). Chosen MDE, n per arm, arms, run length, with and without CUPED.

docs.title: 7. Analysis plan
docs.text:
Primary test. Estimator, variance estimator (HC3 robust / cluster-robust on what), interval type. "Two-proportion z-test on triggered users, cross-checked with OLS + HC3."

Covariate adjustment / CUPED. Which pre-treatment covariate, why it is pre-treatment, and the expected variance reduction.

correction_family — the multiple-testing families, declared now. Which tests belong to which family and which correction applies. Default: no correction for the single OEC; Bonferroni across the guardrail family; Benjamini–Hochberg for any segment sweep.

Pre-registered segments (if any). List them now or do not claim them later. A segment discovered after the fact is a hypothesis, not a finding.

stopping_rule. Default: fixed horizon; no interim stopping for significance. If you intend to monitor continuously, name the sequential method that makes it valid.

Validity checks that must pass before the effect is even read. SRM at α = 0.001; balance table with all |SMD| < 0.1; sanity checks on the trigger rate.

What I will do if the experiment is invalid. Say it now, while it costs nothing to say.

docs.title: 8. The observational arm (reminder pilot)
docs.text:
Question and estimand.

Method and why it fits. DiD / matching / IV — and the first question: could we have randomised going forward? If yes, say why we did not.

Identifying assumption, in one sentence. Parallel trends / unconfoundedness given X / exclusion restriction. The exact sentence you will be asked to say out loud.

How the assumption is supported (or why it cannot be). Event study on pre-period coefficients / post-matching balance and overlap / first-stage F.

The single unmeasured variable that would break this.

The ≥ 2 refutation or validation checks I will run, named before I run them.

# Check What result would worry me 1 2

docs.title: 9. Freeze
docs.text:
Run this before any results cell:

from causal_utils import AnalysisPlan, freeze_plan

plan = AnalysisPlan(
    experiment_name="...",
    decision="...",
    randomisation_unit="...",
    oec="...",
    guardrails=["...", "...", "..."],
    trigger_definition="...",
    unit_of_analysis="...",
    mde=0.0,
    alpha=0.05,
    power=0.80,
    planned_n_per_arm=None,
    planned_run_days=None,
    correction_family="...",
    stopping_rule="fixed horizon; no interim stopping for significance",
    practical_threshold=0.01,
)
plan = freeze_plan(plan)
print(plan.to_json())

Paste what it printed:

Field Value frozen_at (UTC) plan_hash Notebook cell number of the freeze First results cell number must be greater than the line above

Signature.

I confirm that this plan was completed and frozen before any outcome data for this experiment was inspected, and that the hash above is the hash of the plan as analysed. Any change made after this point is recorded in §10.

Name: ____ Date: ______

Plan hash: ________

This hash goes in the decision memo. A reader who recomputes it should get the same 16 characters.

docs.title: 10. Amendments after the freeze
docs.text:
Leave this empty if nothing changed. If something did, an honest entry here costs you far less than a silent edit.

Date What changed Why Effect on the conclusion

docs.title: Capstone Self-Audit Checklist
docs.text:
SDA-DSC-213 · Injaz (إنجاز) · SDAIA Academy Complete before submission at milestone M-D (Day 4, H4 end · 13:30).

Every item is answerable yes or no. Answer honestly — a "no" you have written down and explained in the memo costs far less than a "no" the assessor finds. Where an item does not apply to your chosen design, write n/a and one clause saying why.

The sections match the rubric criteria and carry their weights.

docs.title: A. Experiment design & analysis plan — 15 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N A1 Is there a written design doc covering all fields of DESIGN_DOC_TEMPLATE.md? A2 Is the randomisation unit stated explicitly (the field the hash is computed on)? A3 Is the choice of that unit justified against the next-finer unit in at least two sentences? A4 Is exactly one OEC named as primary? A5 Is the OEC defined operationally (numerator, denominator, time window)? A6 Are there at least three guardrails, each with the direction that would alarm you? A7 Is the trigger defined operationally, and is the analysis population the triggered one? A8 Is the unit of analysis stated, and does it match the randomisation unit (or is clustering used)? A9 Is the estimand named (ATE / ATT / LATE / CATE), with the population and window? A10 Was freeze_plan() run before any cell that computes an outcome? A11 Is the frozen plan_hash recorded in the design doc and reproduced in the memo? A12 Does the notebook's freeze cell appear at a lower cell number than the first results cell? A13 Is the SUTVA / interference audit present with two plausible violations and the design change each implies? A14 If anything in the plan changed after the freeze, is it recorded in the amendments table with its effect on the conclusion? A15 Can you say "no metric in this analysis was chosen after I saw an outcome" without qualification?

docs.title: B. Power & sample sizing — 15 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N B1 Is a baseline rate stated, taken from the pre-period rather than from the running experiment? B2 Is the MDE stated as an absolute effect, in the same units as the OEC? B3 Is the required per-arm sample size computed and shown? B4 Is the arm multiplier applied (total traffic = n per arm × number of arms)? B5 Is the trigger rate applied to daily traffic (daily usable = eligible × trigger)? B6 Is the run length rounded up to whole weeks, with a sentence on why weekday and weekend users differ? B7 Is the relationship between MDE and n stated or shown (halving the MDE roughly quadruples n)? B8 Is a CUPED alternative computed with a pre-treatment covariate? B9 Is the variance reduction from CUPED quantified as a percentage? B10 Is the CUPED saving expressed in days or in sample, not just as a percentage? B11 If the observed run is shorter than the plan required, is the under-run named and its consequence stated? B12 Is the MDE compared to the practical threshold, with a sentence on what a null result could and could not rule out?

docs.title: C. Experiment integrity — 10 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N C1 Is assignment deterministic (hash + fixed salt), so the same id always maps to the same arm? C2 Is the salt string recorded in the design doc? C3 Was an SRM check run, with the chi-square statistic and p-value printed? C4 Is the SRM verdict stated in words ("passes / experiment invalid"), not just as a number? C5 Is a covariate-balance table printed, with SMD per covariate (categoricals expanded per level)? C6 Is the worst |SMD| reported and compared to the 0.1 threshold? C7 If a covariate is imbalanced, is the response adjust in analysis rather than re-randomise? C8 Can you confirm you did not re-randomise or re-roll any assignment? C9 If any dataset you analysed fails SRM, is it reported as invalid and not analysed for effect? C10 Is the trigger rate reported, and does the triggered sample size match what the run length predicted?

docs.title: D. A/B analysis correctness — 20 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N D1 Is the effect estimated on triggered users, not on all assigned users? D2 If an all-assigned number also appears, is it labelled as intention-to-treat for a different question? D3 Is the variance robust (HC3) or cluster-robust, not the default OLS standard error? D4 If the analysis rows are finer than the randomisation unit (e.g. sessions), are standard errors clustered on that unit? D5 Is a 95% confidence interval reported alongside every point estimate? D6 Is CUPED applied with a covariate that is unambiguously pre-treatment? D7 Did the CUPED interval get narrower (if it widened, was the cause diagnosed)? D8 Are the guardrails tested as a family, with the correction named (Bonferroni or equivalent) and m stated? D9 Is any segment sweep corrected with Benjamini–Hochberg, and are survivors labelled as hypotheses for a future test rather than findings? D10 Are no post-treatment variables included as covariates anywhere in the A/B analysis? D11 Is the effect compared to the practical threshold, not only to zero? D12 Does the write-up contain both verdicts explicitly: statistical ("is it there") and practical ("is it big enough")? D13 Was the analysis run once at the frozen horizon, with no stopping at first significance? D14 Are percentages and percentage points used correctly and distinguished in every sentence?

docs.title: E. Causal evaluation — 20 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N E1 Is the observational question stated with its own estimand? E2 Is there a DAG (drawn or written as an edge list), with each arrow justified in one line? E3 Is the identifying assumption written out as a single sentence you could say out loud? E4 Is the adjustment set derived from the DAG (backdoor criterion), not chosen by convenience? E5 Have you confirmed that no mediator is in the adjustment set? E6 Have you confirmed that no collider and no descendant of the treatment is in the adjustment set? E7 DiD path: is an event study plotted, with pre-activation coefficients shown? E8 DiD path: are the pre-period coefficients assessed in words — flat and supporting parallel trends, or not flat and therefore not identified? E9 DiD path: are standard errors clustered on the panel unit? E10 DiD path: is the staggered-rollout caveat acknowledged (TWFE weights, ramp-in attenuation)? E11 Matching path: is propensity overlap / common support shown and any trimming reported? E12 Matching path: is a post-matching balance table shown with all |SMD| < 0.1? E13 Matching path: are unmatched treated units counted, and is the estimand restated if many were dropped? E14 Matching path: is a sensitivity analysis (e.g. Rosenbaum bounds) reported with the Γ at which the conclusion flips? E15 Are at least two refutation or validation checks run, and were they named in the plan before they were run? E16 Is the result of each refutation stated, including any that did not pass? E17 Is the single unmeasured variable that would break the estimate named? E18 If the estimate is not identified, is that reported as the finding rather than worked around? E19 If the experimental and observational estimates disagree, is the gap explained through a specific assumption rather than one number being dropped?

docs.title: F. Decision communication — 15 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N F1 Is the memo one page? F2 Is there a recommendation per intervention in the first five lines? F3 Is each recommendation one of ship / scale / hold-and-extend / stop, stated as a verb? F4 Are effects reported in business units (percentage points, and completions per month where useful)? F5 Is a confidence interval reported for every effect, and translated into business units too? F6 Are there no p-values in the body of the memo (validity checks such as SRM excepted)? F7 Is the practical threshold stated, and is the interval compared to it explicitly? F8 Are the key assumptions stated as risks, with consequences? F9 Is there an explicit "what would change this" with a specific, costed next step? F10 Does the decision plot show the effects, their intervals and the threshold line? F11 Is the plan hash in the memo header? F12 Would a non-technical reader get the recommendation and its main caveat from the first paragraph alone? F13 Do the caveats run in both directions, rather than all conveniently supporting one conclusion? F14 Is any null result phrased as "not distinguishable from zero at this sample" rather than "there was no effect"?

docs.title: G. Reproducibility & integrity — 5 points
docs.text: # Question Y / N G1 Does the notebook run top to bottom on a clean kernel without errors? G2 Is a random seed fixed and set once, near the top? G3 Are all data paths relative, so the notebook runs on another machine? G4 Are outputs present in the submitted notebook (not cleared)? G5 Does the plan hash in the notebook match the plan hash in the memo? G6 Is every optional-dependency cell (DoWhy / EconML) either runnable or clearly marked optional with a core-stack equivalent beside it? G7 Is the analysis free of any peeking-driven stopping decision? G8 Is all work your own, with reuse limited to causal_utils and your own Lab 1–7 code?

docs.title: H. Extension — up to +5 bonus (only if mandatory scope ≥ 80)
docs.text: # Question Y / N H1 Is at least one extension from the brief attempted? H2 Is the extension's result reported with uncertainty, not as a point estimate? H3 CATE: is the multiple-testing problem across subgroups addressed explicitly? H4 Sequential: is the always-valid bound contrasted with the fixed-horizon interval? H5 Staggered DiD: is the cohort-aware estimate compared with naive TWFE, with the difference explained? H6 IV: are all three conditions argued and the first-stage F reported (with F < 10 flagged as unreliable)? H7 Power study: is the saving expressed in run days for a future Injaz experiment? H8 Does the extension change or confirm the recommendation, and does the memo say which?

docs.title: Final gate — the four questions asked live
docs.text:
You will be asked these in your 6-minute briefing. If you cannot answer any one of them in a sentence, go back before you submit.

# Question Y / N — can I answer this in one sentence? 1 What is the identifying assumption behind your causal estimate? 2 What single unmeasured variable would break it? 3 What would change your recommendation, and what would it cost to find out? 4 Which number in your memo are you least confident about, and why?

docs.title: Count your "no"s
docs.text:
• Zero "no"s in sections C, D and E is the bar for the top band on those criteria.
  • Any "no" in section A10–A12 (the freeze) caps criterion 1 and endangers criterion 7.
  • Any "no" that you keep must appear in the memo as a stated limitation. A declared weakness is a scored strength; an undeclared one is an anti-pattern flag.

docs.title: Injaz (إنجاز) Course Datasets — Data Dictionary
docs.text:
SDA-DSC-213 · Experimentation, A/B Testing and Causal Inference · SDAIA Academy

All data is synthetic, generated by make_data.py. No real citizen or government data is used anywhere in this course. Ground-truth effects are planted so every method can be checked against a number that was deliberately put there — see GROUND_TRUTH.json.

Regenerate everything with:

cd data && python make_data.py

docs.title: The scenario
docs.text:
Injaz is a unified Saudi digital-government services platform: citizens renew licences, issue certificates, update addresses and pay fees online. Three threads run through the whole course:

Thread Question Method Days Guided uploader Does a redesigned document-upload step raise service completion? randomised A/B test 1–2 Regional reminders Did the region-by-region reminder rollout raise completion? difference-in-differences 3 Digital-literacy training Did the voluntary training programme help those who took it? matching / IPW 3 AI autofill Should we launch autofill nationally? capstone A/B + causal evaluation 4

docs.title: simulated_potential_outcomes.parquet — 20,000 rows · Module 1
docs.text:
The only file in the course containing both potential outcomes for every unit. This is impossible in reality, which is precisely why the course starts here: you can watch an estimator succeed or fail against a truth you can see.

Column Type Meaning user_id int Unit identifier region, age, device, device_age_years, distance_km, prior_sessions, prior_completion_rate, digital_literacy_score, signup_cohort mixed Baseline covariates latent_literacy float The true confounder (exposed only in this teaching file) y0 0/1 Y(0) — completion if not given the uploader y1 0/1 Y(1) — completion if given the uploader tau_individual int Y(1) − Y(0), the individual effect. Never observable in practice treated_self_selected 0/1 Opt-in assignment (confounded by literacy) treated_randomised 0/1 Coin-flip assignment y_observed_self_selected 0/1 What you would actually see under opt-in y_observed_randomised 0/1 What you would actually see under randomisation p_select float P(opt in), the selection mechanism

Planted truth: ATE = +5.04 pp. Naive self-selected comparison = +19.30 pp (selection bias ≈ +14.32 pp). Naive randomised comparison ≈ +5.04 pp.

docs.title: injaz_users_pool.csv — 200,000 rows · Module 2
docs.text:
The eligible user pool for assignment, SRM and balance work. No outcomes — this file is used before an experiment runs.

Key columns: user_id, region, age, device, os_family, device_age_years, distance_km, prior_sessions, prior_completion_rate, digital_literacy_score, signup_cohort, preferred_language, is_eligible.

docs.title: injaz_users.csv — 20,000 rows · Modules 5 & 6
docs.text:
The observational analysis cohort. Carries three separate causal stories:

Column Meaning enrolled_training 0/1 — self-selected into the digital-literacy programme online_filing 0/1 — endogenous choice of filing channel log_distance_km log km to the nearest service centre — the instrument for online_filing support_calls count — a mediator/collider trap: downstream of both treatment and outcome completed 0/1 — the outcome

Planted truths: ATT of training = +6.0 pp (naive difference ≈ +11.5 pp). LATE of online filing = +8.0 pp (OLS biased to ≈ +10.9 pp; first-stage F ≈ 2,100).

Use log_distance_km, not distance_km, as the instrument. Raw kilometres are heavily right-skewed and the first stage is mis-specified in levels — a useful five-minute exercise in its own right.

docs.title: injaz_experiment_results.csv — 80,000 rows · Modules 2 & 4
docs.text:
The guided-uploader randomised experiment, user-level.

Column Meaning variant control / treatment — the randomised arm triggered 0/1 — did the user reach the document-upload step at all? exposed 0/1 — treatment and triggered completed 0/1 — the OEC support_contact, session_duration_sec, error_flag, drop_off the guardrail family prior_completion_rate pre-experiment covariate — the CUPED variable region, device, age_band, signup_cohort segmentation

Planted truth: +2.2 pp on completion among triggered users. Analysing all 80,000 assigned users instead of the 49,653 triggered ones dilutes the effect by roughly the trigger rate (+2.16 pp becomes +1.34 pp) — a deliberate trap.

docs.title: injaz_experiment_results_srm_broken.csv — 78,747 rows
docs.text: The same experiment with ~3% of the treatment arm silently dropped. SRM chi-square ≈ 16.5, p ≈ 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ → the experiment is invalid and must not be analysed. Used for the SRM injector demo.

docs.title: injaz_pre_period.csv — 50,000 rows · Module 3
docs.text:
Pre-experiment window for CUPED: user_id, pre_sessions, pre_completion_rate, pre_avg_duration_sec.

Planted truth: corr(pre_completion_rate, post-period completed) ≈ 0.37 → CUPED variance reduction ≈ 13.5%, i.e. ~1.16× the effective sample for free.

docs.title: injaz_traffic_forecast.csv — 90 rows · Module 3
docs.text: Daily eligible traffic for run-length planning: date, day_of_week, eligible_users, trigger_rate, is_weekend. Follows the KSA working week (Fri–Sat are ~58% of a weekday), which is exactly why run lengths must be whole weeks.

docs.title: injaz_sessions.csv.gz — 339,017 rows · Modules 2 & 4
docs.text:
Session-level events, ~4.2 sessions per user. Outcomes are correlated within user, so a session-level analysis of a user-randomised experiment produces standard errors that are far too small. That is the point of the file.

Columns: session_id, user_id, session_start, region, device, service_type, variant, triggered_uploader, exposed_uploader, session_completed, duration_sec.

triggered_uploader = the session reached the document-upload step, and it is present in both arms (about 49.7% of control sessions and 49.6% of treatment sessions). exposed_uploader = reached that step and was in the treatment arm. Filtering the clustering demo on triggered_uploader is therefore legitimate: both arms survive the filter.

docs.title: injaz_regions_panel.csv — 312 rows (13 regions × 24 months) · Module 5
docs.text:
The staggered reminder rollout.

Column Meaning activation_month period the region switched on (blank = never treated) treated_ever, post, treated_post DiD indicators months_since_activation relative time for the event study completion_rate, completions, eligible_users, reminders_sent outcomes and volume

Activation waves: periods 10, 13, 16, 19; 4 regions never treated.

Planted truth: full ATT = +3.0 pp, with a two-month ramp-in (60% of the effect in the first two months). TWFE therefore recovers ≈ +2.6 pp — the attenuation is real, not a bug, and is the opening for the staggered-DiD extension in the capstone.

docs.title: injaz_regions_panel_pretrend.csv — 312 rows
docs.text: Identical, except treated regions are given a divergent pre-trend. The event study shows non-zero pre-period coefficients and parallel trends fails. Used for the parallel-trends-breaker simulation.

docs.title: collider_sim.parquet — 50,000 rows · Module 6
docs.text:
Two independent causes (digital_literacy, service_simplicity) of one collider (completed).

Planted truth: unconditional correlation ≈ 0.00; conditional on completed == 1 it becomes ≈ −0.20. Nothing changed in the world — only the rows you looked at.

docs.title: injaz_autofill_ab.csv — 70,000 rows · Capstone
docs.text:
The AI-assisted autofill experiment. Same structure as the uploader experiment.

Planted truth: +1.4 pp on completion among triggered users (49,510 of the 70,000 assigned trigger, a rate of 70.7%), against a 1.0 pp practical-significance threshold. Analysing all 70,000 assigned users instead dilutes +1.37 pp to +0.97 pp — the trigger rate times the planted lift. The confidence interval is designed to straddle that threshold: the effect is real and statistically significant, yet the data cannot establish that it is large enough to justify the build. The correct capstone answer is a hold / extend, not a ship — and a participant who writes "p < 0.05, ship it" has missed the entire course.

docs.title: Answer Key
docs.text:
SDA-DSC-213 · Experimentation, A/B Testing and Causal Inference · SDAIA Academy Instructor document — do not distribute.

Every number in this document was computed from the shipped datasets with the shipped causal_utils. If a participant's number differs by more than the stated tolerance, something is wrong with their analysis, not with the data — unless python environment_check.py fails its ground-truth smoke tests, in which case the seeds have moved and this whole document needs regenerating.

How to use the tolerances. They are set so that a correct analysis with a defensible variation in method (two-proportion versus OLS+HC3, matching with a slightly different caliper, a different covariate list) lands inside, while the three deliberate traps in §6 land outside. A number outside tolerance is a prompt to ask "which rows did you analyse, and what did you control for?" — in that order, because those two questions explain almost every miss.

docs.title: 1. The planted truths at a glance
docs.text:
Source of truth: data/GROUND_TRUTH.json, written by data/make_data.py.

Quantity Planted Realised in the shipped sample Where it is recovered Uploader ATE (simulator) +5.04 pp +5.04 pp Lab 1 Naive self-selected comparison — +19.30 pp Lab 1 Selection-bias term — +14.32 pp Lab 1 Uploader A/B lift, triggered users +2.2 pp +2.16 pp Labs 2, 4 Trigger rate, uploader — 62.07% Labs 2, 4 Training programme ATT +6.0 pp +6.48 pp matched · naive +11.54 pp Lab 5a Reminder rollout ATT +3.0 pp +2.61 pp TWFE (ramp-in attenuation) Lab 5b Online-filing LATE +8.0 pp +7.78 pp 2SLS · OLS +10.9 pp Lab 6 / extension First-stage F (log_distance_km) — ≈ 2,120 Lab 6 / extension Collider correlation 0.00 → strongly negative −0.0005 → −0.204 Lab 6 Autofill lift, triggered users +1.4 pp +1.37 pp, CI straddles the +1.0 pp threshold Lab 7, capstone CUPED variance reduction — ≈ 13.5% (ρ ≈ 0.37) Lab 3, Lab 4 Peeking FPR at 20 looks — ≈ 25% (nominal 5%) Lab 4

docs.title: 2. Lab by lab — what should be recovered
Lab 1 — Potential outcomes and selection bias
docs.text:
Data: simulated_potential_outcomes.parquet (20,000 rows)

Quantity Expected Tolerance Note True ATE (tau_individual.mean()) +0.0504 ±0.002 It is exactly this number; the file contains both potential outcomes Naive, self-selected +0.1930 ±0.005 Naive, randomised +0.0504 ±0.008 Wider tolerance: a participant who re-randomises with their own seed gets a different draw Selection-bias term E[Y(0)|T=1] − E[Y(0)|T=0] +0.1432 ±0.005 ATT under self-selection +0.0498 ±0.005 Nearly equal to the ATE here — the treatment effect is homogeneous, only selection differs Convergence sweep at n = 1M converges to 0.193 — The point of the lab: it converges to the biased value, not to 0.050

Identity to check: naive (0.1930) ≈ ATT (0.0498) + bias (0.1432) = 0.1930. If a participant's three numbers do not add up, they revealed the wrong potential outcome — check observed = where(T==1, y1, y0).

docs.title: Lab 2 — Design and randomise
docs.text:
Data: injaz_users_pool.csv (200,000 rows; 182,113 eligible), injaz_experiment_results_srm_broken.csv

Quantity Expected Tolerance Hash split with salt="injaz-uploader-2026q2" ≈ 50/50, stable across reruns allocation 0.50 ± 0.005 SRM on the clean assignment passes, p ≈ 0.61 any p ≥ 0.001 SRM on injaz_experiment_results.csv passes: χ² = 0.16, p = 0.692 — SRM on the broken file FAILS: χ² = 16.53, p = 4.78 × 10⁻⁵, treatment −1.45% any p far below 0.001 Balance table, worst |SMD| 0.013 (uploader file, 21 covariate cells) < 0.10 Frozen plan a 16-character plan_hash exists —

Reference frozen plan: notebooks/lab2_frozen_plan.json, hash b47e305fe7c01612. A participant's hash will differ — the hash covers the timestamp and their own wording. What matters is that a hash exists and was produced before any results cell.

The broken file, for reference. DATA_DICTIONARY.md and this table now agree: 78,747 rows, χ² = 16.53, p = 4.78 × 10⁻⁵, treatment arm 1.45% light. The teaching point is unchanged — the experiment is emphatically invalid. Use the numbers in this table.

docs.title: Lab 3 — Sizing and run length
docs.text:
Data: injaz_pre_period.csv (50,000 rows), injaz_traffic_forecast.csv (90 days)

Quantity Expected Tolerance n per arm (p = 0.55, MDE = 0.02, 80% power, α = 0.05) 9,669 ±150; statsmodels must agree n per arm (MDE = 0.01) 38,769 ±600 n per arm (MDE = 0.005) 155,246 ±2,500 Mean daily eligible traffic 13,410 — Mean trigger rate in the forecast 0.620 — Daily usable units (eligible × trigger) 8,319 ±50 Weekend traffic as a share of weekday 58% (8,896 vs 15,244) — MDE detectable in 4 weeks, 2 arms, at live traffic 0.0059 ±0.0005 corr(pre_completion_rate, post completed) 0.367 ±0.02 CUPED variance reduction 13.5% ±2 pp Effective sample multiplier from CUPED 1.16× ±0.05

Run lengths (2 arms unless stated), using 13,410 eligible/day × 0.620 trigger:

MDE n/arm Days by arithmetic Recommended (whole weeks, floor 14) 0.02 9,669 3 14 0.02, 3 arms 9,669 4 14 0.01 38,769 10 14 0.005 155,246 38 42 0.005, 3 arms 155,246 56 56

Teaching note. Labs 3 and 7 call run_length(..., floor_days=14): the KSA working week means a run must cover whole weeks, and two of them, so that both weekday and weekend users are sampled in proportion. At MDE = 0.02 the arm multiplier is therefore invisible — both 2 and 3 arms sit on the 14-day floor. Have the room rerun at MDE = 0.005, where 2 arms needs 42 days and 3 arms needs 56, and the multiplier is unmissable.

Catalogue discrepancy. The instructor package's illustrative Lab 3 output quotes n = 9,873, an achievable MDE of 0.0091, run lengths of 14 and 21 days, and a CUPED reduction of 42%. Those were written against different traffic assumptions and a different pre-period covariate. The shipped data gives the numbers in the tables above; a 42% CUPED reduction on this data means the participant used a post-treatment covariate.

docs.title: Lab 4 — Analyse the uploader experiment
docs.text:
Data: injaz_experiment_results.csv (80,000 assigned; 49,653 triggered), injaz_pre_period.csv, injaz_sessions.csv.gz

Quantity Expected Tolerance Lift on triggered users (two-proportion) +2.16 pp, 95% CI [+1.29, +3.04], p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ estimate ±0.3 pp Same, OLS + HC3 identical point estimate must match to 3 dp n per arm, triggered 24,838 treatment / 24,815 control — Control-arm baseline completion (triggered) 55.37% — CUPED-adjusted lift +2.07 pp, CI [+1.26, +2.88] ±0.3 pp; CI must be narrower CUPED variance reduction 13.5% ±2 pp Peeking FPR 1 look 5.1% · 5 looks 14.3% · 10 looks 20.2% · 20 looks 25.4% ±3 pp Session-level, unclustered +0.86 pp, CI [+0.53, +1.18] — ±0.33 pp, too narrow — Session-level, clustered on user_id +0.86 pp, CI [+0.33, +1.38] — ±0.52 pp, honest same point estimate, wider CI

Guardrail family, Bonferroni m = 4:

Guardrail Effect Raw p Bonferroni p Verdict session_duration_sec +4.42 s 4.8 × 10⁻⁸ 1.9 × 10⁻⁷ Rises, and survives the correction drop_off −1.56 pp 1.7 × 10⁻⁴ 6.9 × 10⁻⁴ Improves — this is the mechanism behind the OEC win support_contact −0.54 pp 1.8 × 10⁻³ 7.3 × 10⁻³ Improves — falls, and survives the correction error_flag +0.03 pp 0.864 1.000 Flat

The uploader is the interesting guardrail case: the one metric that moves against us survives the family correction, and is still not material. A participant who never tests session_duration_sec at all has skipped the family; a participant who reports "significant, therefore a breach" has skipped the business threshold. The correct write-up says the feature raises completion by 2.2 pp at a cost of about 4.4 seconds on a 159-second baseline — a 2.8% rise, statistically unambiguous on 49,653 users and a business judgement rather than a statistic. The frozen plan said "must not rise materially"; 4.4 s is not material, and the memo should say so explicitly rather than dropping the row.

Segment sweep. With 16 region × device tests, expect a handful of raw-significant results, few of which survive Benjamini–Hochberg (7 and 1 respectively on the shipped file). The exact count depends on the segment definition, so do not mark against a number: mark against whether BH was applied and whether survivors were labelled as hypotheses for a future test rather than as findings.

docs.title: Lab 5a — Matching, the training programme
docs.text:
Data: injaz_users.csv (20,000 rows; enrolment rate 46.3%)

Quantity Expected Tolerance Naive difference +11.54 pp ±0.3 pp Worst |SMD| before matching 0.566 ±0.05 Worst |SMD| after matching 0.032 must be < 0.10 Matched ATT +6.48 pp, CI [+5.06, +7.90] ±1.0 pp — the planted truth is +6.0 pp Stabilised IPW ATE +6.62 pp, CI [+5.15, +8.09] ±1.0 pp Matched treated units 9,262 of 9,263 (caliper 0.02) at most one dropped Rosenbaum Γ* survives Γ = 1.20, fails at Γ = 1.25 ±1 grid step Random-common-cause refutation estimate shifts by < 0.02 pp — passes Subset refutation (70%, 10 draws) mean +6.79 pp, sd 0.58 pp — passes Placebo outcome distance_km effect +0.28, p = 0.058 — passes

The covariate list matters more than the matching algorithm. A participant who omits digital_literacy_score lands at +9.14 pp, most of the way back to the naive +11.5 pp, because that is the variable driving selection. This is the right teaching moment: matching removes bias only from the confounders you measured.

A trap inside a refutation. placebo_outcome_test fails if the placebo outcome is also in the adjustment set — prior_completion_rate returns an effect of −3 × 10⁻¹⁶ with a p-value of 3 × 10⁻¹¹, which is a numerical artefact of perfect collinearity, not evidence. Excluded from the adjustment set the same placebo comes back clean (effect +0.0035, p = 0.13), so the artefact is the only thing the in-set version was ever detecting. Use distance_km as the placebo outcome. Expect at least one pair to hit this; it is a good five minutes.

docs.title: Lab 5b — DiD, the regional reminder rollout
docs.text:
Data: injaz_regions_panel.csv (13 regions × 24 months = 312 rows; waves at periods 10, 13, 16, 19; 4 never-treated regions)

Quantity Expected Tolerance TWFE DiD, region-clustered +2.61 pp, 95% CI [+2.48, +2.74] ±0.4 pp Planted ATT +3.00 pp — Event study, pre-period coefficients (rel −6 … −2) all within ±0.5 pp of zero; none significant; max |coef| = 0.42 pp all CIs cover 0 Event study, rel 0 and +1 (ramp-in) +2.06 pp, +1.64 pp — mean +1.85 pp ±0.5 pp Event study, rel ≥ +2 (mature) mean +3.26 pp ±0.5 pp — this is the planted +3.0 pp after ramp-in Placebo timing (activation shifted earlier) null CI covers 0

Pre-trend-broken file (injaz_regions_panel_pretrend.csv):

Quantity Expected Naive TWFE +4.24 pp, CI [+3.27, +5.20] — inflated Pre-period coefficients −1.64, −0.53, −0.91, −0.34, −0.14 pp — clearly non-zero and trending Correct verdict parallel trends fails; DiD is not identified here. Report the failure.

docs.title: Lab 6 — DAGs, colliders, identification
docs.text:
Data: injaz_users.csv, collider_sim.parquet (50,000 rows)

Quantity Expected Tolerance Minimal backdoor adjustment set {digital_literacy, device_age} exact support_calls classification mediator / descendant — excluded exact Collider correlation, unconditional −0.0005 ±0.01 Collider correlation, conditional on completed == 1 −0.204 ±0.02 Collider correlation, conditional on completed == 0 −0.193 ±0.02 Backdoor paths listed by InjazDAG.backdoor_paths() 4 exact

IV (Lab 6 extension / capstone): with log_distance_km as the instrument and digital_literacy_score as an exogenous control —

Quantity Expected Tolerance 2SLS LATE +7.78 pp, CI [+3.05, +12.51] ±2.5 pp; planted +8.0 pp OLS (biased) +10.89 pp ±0.5 pp First-stage F ≈ 2,120 far above 10 either way

With no exogenous controls the LATE is +6.16 pp (CI [+1.29, +11.03]) and the OLS comparison is +12.91 pp; GROUND_TRUTH.json records +7.89 pp, which is the specification that controls for measured literacy. Accept anything in +5 to +9 pp with a defended specification. The graded content is the three IV conditions and the first-stage F, not the third decimal.

Use log_distance_km, never distance_km. Raw kilometres are heavily right-skewed and the first stage is mis-specified in levels — a useful five-minute exercise in its own right.

docs.title: Lab 7 and the capstone — the autofill decision
docs.text:
Data: injaz_autofill_ab.csv (70,000 assigned; 49,510 triggered; trigger rate 70.7%)

Quantity Expected Tolerance Lift on triggered users +1.37 pp, 95% CI [+0.49, +2.24], p = 0.0022 ±0.3 pp CUPED-adjusted (or OLS + prior_completion_rate) +1.57 pp, CI [+0.76, +2.38] ±0.3 pp; CI must be narrower n per arm, triggered 24,736 treatment / 24,774 control — Control-arm baseline completion (triggered) 55.06% — SRM passes: 35,016 control vs 34,984 treatment, χ² = 0.01, p = 0.90 p ≥ 0.001 Balance, worst |SMD| 0.019 across 21 covariate cells < 0.10 Practical-significance threshold +1.0 pp (given by the programme board) — Correct verdict HOLD / EXTEND — the CI straddles +1.0 pp —

Guardrail family, Bonferroni m = 4:

Guardrail Effect Raw p Bonferroni p Verdict session_duration_sec −10.43 s ≈ 0 ≈ 0 Improves drop_off −1.34 pp 0.0013 0.0053 Improves — survives the correction error_flag −0.25 pp 0.102 0.406 Not significant after correction support_contact +0.19 pp 0.283 1.000 Not significant, before or after correction

The reminder half of the capstone uses the Lab 5b numbers: +2.61 pp, CI [+2.48, +2.74], entirely above the +1.0 pp threshold → SCALE, with the parallel-trends caveat and the note that TWFE understates the mature effect.

"What would change this" — the number to expect. To move the lower bound of the autofill interval above +1.0 pp requires a standard error below 0.00291 (they have 0.00413 CUPED-adjusted), which is about 2.0× the sample: roughly 50,000 additional triggered users, about 7 running days at 8,319 triggered users per day. Accept anything in the range "about one more week / roughly twice the sample". A participant who says "collect more data" without a number has not answered the question.

docs.title: 3. Where each capstone requirement is recovered
docs.text: Requirement Expected evidence Key number 1 · Design frozen plan with a hash, produced before results any 16-char hash, cell order verified 2 · Power n/arm, arms, trigger, whole-week floor, CUPED saving see the Lab 3 table 3 · Integrity SRM χ² = 0.01, p = 0.90; worst |SMD| = 0.019 both must appear 4 · Analysis +1.37 pp, CI [+0.49, +2.24]; CUPED +1.57 pp, CI [+0.76, +2.38]; guardrails Bonferroni m = 4 verdict must be HOLD/EXTEND 5 · Causal DiD +2.61 pp, CI [+2.48, +2.74]; flat pre-trends; ≥ 2 refutations or matched ATT +6.48 pp with Γ* ≈ 1.20–1.25 6 · Communication one-page memo, effects + CIs in business units ≈ +4,400 completions/month, 2,100–6,600 7 · Reproducibility clean seeded run; plan hash matches between notebook and memo —

docs.title: 4. The three deliberate traps
docs.text: Each trap is a real analytical error, planted so that falling in produces a plausible number rather than an obviously broken one. That is what makes them teachable: the participant cannot tell they are wrong by looking at the output.

docs.title: Trap 1 — analysing all assigned users instead of triggered users
docs.text:
Where it bites. Lab 4, Lab 7 and the capstone. It is the most common error in the course and the most common error in industry.

Why it is plausible. The all-assigned number is smaller but still positive and still highly significant. Nothing looks broken.

Uploader experiment (injaz_experiment_results.csv):

Correct — triggered Trap — all assigned n per arm 24,838 / 24,815 40,056 / 39,944 Effect +2.16 pp +1.34 pp 95% CI [+1.29, +3.04] [+0.65, +2.03] p 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ Matches the planted +2.2 pp? yes no — diluted by the trigger rate: 0.6207 × 2.16 = 1.34

Autofill experiment (injaz_autofill_ab.csv), where the trap changes the verdict:

Correct — triggered Trap — all assigned n per arm 24,736 / 24,774 34,984 / 35,016 Effect +1.37 pp +0.97 pp 95% CI [+0.49, +2.24] [+0.23, +1.70] Distance from the +1.0 pp threshold point estimate 0.4 pp above point estimate 0.03 pp below Effect on the memo HOLD/EXTEND, with a real effect that may or may not clear the bar the diluted point estimate now sits under the bar, so a participant who ran it reads "real but too small" and recommends stopping. Same data, opposite decision

The arithmetic is exact: trigger rate 0.7073 × the planted +1.40 pp = +0.99 pp, and the observed all-assigned figure is +0.968 pp. Put that multiplication on the board — it is the cleanest demonstration of the trap in the whole course.

The built-in A/A test. In both experiments the non-triggered stratum is a clean null by construction: −0.007 pp on the uploader and +0.007 pp on autofill. Those users cannot have been affected by a feature they never reached, so the stratum doubles as an A/A test on the randomisation itself. Have participants estimate the effect on triggered == 0 and read the ±0.01 pp back: it shows the dilution is arithmetic, not noise, and it validates the assignment at the same time.

How to spot it. Check the reported n. Triggered n per arm is ≈ 24,800 (uploader) or ≈ 24,750 (autofill); all-assigned is ≈ 40,000 or ≈ 35,000. The sample size gives the trap away instantly, and on both files the estimate confirms it: the diluted figure is the correct one multiplied by the trigger rate.

The fix, and the thing to say. Filter on triggered == 1. Then add the nuance: the all-assigned number is not meaningless, it is the intention-to-treat estimate, which answers "what happens if we ship this to everyone, including the people who never see it?" That is a legitimate question — it is just not the one that was asked, and reporting it as "the effect of the feature" is wrong. A participant who reports both, correctly labelled, is performing above the bar.

docs.title: Trap 2 — controlling for the support_calls mediator
docs.text:
Where it bites. Lab 6 Task 5, PA-2, and any capstone regression where a participant adds "sensible" controls.

Why it is plausible. support_calls correlates with completion and with digital literacy. It looks exactly like a confounder to anyone who has not drawn the DAG. Adding it changes the estimate by only about one percentage point, so the result still looks reasonable.

Why it is wrong. In the data-generating process, support_calls is drawn after the outcome: it depends on latent literacy and on 1 − completed. It is downstream of both the treatment and the outcome — a mediator on one path and a collider on another. Conditioning on it blocks part of the causal path and opens a spurious one. Two errors, one variable.

Online-filing effect (adjusting for digital_literacy_score and device_age_years):

Specification Estimate What happened Correct adjustment set +10.90 pp the backdoor-adjusted estimate + support_calls +9.77 pp 10% of the effect erased

Training-programme effect (same adjustment set):

Specification Estimate What happened Correct adjustment set +6.92 pp close to the planted +6.0 pp ATT + support_calls +6.11 pp 12% of the effect erased

How to spot it. Look for support_calls in any smf.ols formula or any covariate list. It is the only post-treatment variable in injaz_users.csv, so it is easy to grep for. In the capstone this caps criterion 5 at 70%.

The fix, and the thing to say. Drop it, and derive the adjustment set from the DAG (InjazDAG(...).minimal_adjustment_set() returns {digital_literacy, device_age} and lists support_calls under "mediators — never adjust for these"). Then connect it to Day 2: this is the same rule as CUPED's pre-treatment requirement. A variable measured after the treatment can absorb the treatment's effect. Pre-treatment covariates remove noise; post-treatment covariates remove signal.

docs.title: Trap 3 — reading the TWFE ramp-in attenuation as the answer
docs.text:
Where it bites. Lab 5b and the capstone's causal-evaluation section.

Why it is plausible. TWFE gives +2.61 pp with a tight interval [+2.48, +2.74] and a p-value indistinguishable from zero. Nothing about the output suggests it is an underestimate. Every diagnostic passes: pre-trends are flat, the placebo is null, the standard errors are clustered.

Why it is an underestimate. The programme was planted with a two-month ramp-in — 60% of the effect lands in the first two months — and it was rolled out in four staggered waves (periods 10, 13, 16, 19). TWFE averages the weak early months in with the mature ones, so the coefficient sits below the mature effect. The event study shows the whole story:

Relative month Coefficient Reading −6 to −2 +0.30, +0.13, −0.14, +0.42, +0.26 pp flat — parallel trends supported −1 0 (baseline) 0 +2.06 pp ramp-in, month 1 +1 +1.64 pp ramp-in, month 2 +2 to +8 +3.38, +3.24, +3.28, +3.41, +3.35, +3.22, +2.94 pp mature: mean +3.26 pp, just above the planted ATT Value Planted ATT +3.00 pp TWFE (the trap, if reported as "the effect") +2.61 pp, CI [+2.48, +2.74] Event-study ramp-in months (rel 0, +1) mean +1.85 pp Event-study mature months (rel ≥ +2) mean +3.26 pp Gap 0.39 pp, and the planted value sits outside the TWFE interval

How to spot it. A participant reports +2.61 pp and stops. The tell is not the number — the number is correct — it is the absence of the event study, or an event study that is plotted and then not read.

The fix, and the thing to say. Reporting +2.61 pp is not wrong; reporting it as "the effect of the reminder programme" without qualification is. Distinction- band work says: "TWFE gives +2.6 pp. The event study shows the programme ramps in over two months and matures at about +3.3 pp; TWFE averages the weak early months in, so +2.6 pp understates the steady-state effect. For a scale decision this error is in the safe direction." That sentence is also the motivation for the staggered-DiD capstone extension, where a Callaway–Sant'Anna or Sun–Abraham estimator recovers the mature effect directly.

Note the direction. Unlike Traps 1 and 2, this one makes the intervention look worse than it is. It is worth saying so — participants learn to expect that all bias is self-serving, and this is the counterexample.

docs.title: 5. Fast triage — a number is off, now what
docs.text: Symptom First thing to check A/B effect is ≈ 1.3 pp instead of 2.2 pp on the uploader Trap 1 — all assigned, not triggered. Check n per arm. Matched ATT is near +9 pp digital_literacy_score missing from the propensity model Any causal estimate is ~1 pp lower than expected Trap 2 — grep the formula for support_calls DiD is +4.2 pp with sloping pre-trends They are using injaz_regions_panel_pretrend.csv — correct answer is "not identified" DiD is +2.6 pp and no event study exists Trap 3 — ask what the mature effect is CUPED reduction ≈ 40% Post-treatment covariate CUPED interval got wider Non-predictive covariate, or leakage Guardrails "all clean" on the uploader session_duration_sec untested — it rises +4.42 s and survives Bonferroni, so it is the business threshold, not the correction, that settles it Every segment is significant No BH correction applied IV estimate wildly imprecise Using distance_km in levels instead of log_distance_km Two participants get different numbers from the same lab Different data-generation runs, or seed set after the first draw Nothing matches this document at all Run python environment_check.py — if the smoke tests fail, the seeds moved and this key is stale
