docs.title: Title: The Masar Mini-Lakehouse — Production Data Platform for a Saudi Mobility Operator
Project Scenario
docs.text: You are the data platform engineer for Masar (مسار), the national smart-mobility operator. The analytics team hands you raw feeds — batch trips and drivers, streaming GPS — and two demands: an AI feature service for an ETA/demand model, and an operations BI dashboard the leadership reviews every morning. Your mandate: deliver a production-grade Mini-Lakehouse that both teams can trust — because the platform proves its own quality, freshness, and governance. Everything you built in Labs 1–8 is a component; the capstone is the integration plus your own extensions.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mandatory (maps to grading rubric):

  1. Medallion architecture (LO1, LO7): bronze (append-only, lineage) → silver (conformed) → gold (marts + feature table); documented layer contracts; no layer bypassed.
  2. Compute–storage discipline (LO2): data in an object-storage-style layout; a short BENCHMARKS.md cost/scan analysis; gold marts OPTIMIZEd/ZORDERed with measured file-count reduction.
  3. ELT pipeline (LO3): dbt (or Spark) staging → silver, incremental merge on trip_id with a lookback window; source-freshness + ≥ 6 data tests; a demonstrated late-arrival backfill.
  4. Delta Lake (LO4): silver as constrained Delta (schema + CHECK); idempotent MERGE upserts; time-travel audit; OPTIMIZE/VACUUM with justified retention; one PDPL erasure demonstrated.
  5. Streaming (LO5): Kafka GPS topic → Structured Streaming → Delta bronze, exactly-once with a dedicated checkpoint; a kill/restart proof of no duplicates; event-time windowed demand with a watermark.
  6. Quality, observability, governance (LO6): Great Expectations suite with fail-fast + quarantine; freshness/volume/drift checks; PII classification + retention job; data docs as evidence.
  7. Orchestration (LO7): the full medallion as one dependency-ordered, idempotent DAG, runnable by one command, with a demonstrated idempotent recovery from an injected mid-DAG failure.
  8. Serving (LO8): a point-in-time-correct feature table served offline + materialised online (consistency proven); a conformed star schema BI mart that reconciles; a PDPL-safe serving view.

One extension (choose at least one): - Offline/online consistency check wired into CI (Redis vs gold for all keys) - A leakage-lint that fails the pipeline if a feature window includes non-prior data - Multi-city backfill (7 days) proving idempotent correctness across the window - A second streaming consumer group powering a live console demand view - Trino/Databricks-SQL direct-serve endpoint benchmarked against the materialised mart

docs.title: Architecture (target state)
docs.text:
sources                         BRONZE            SILVER             GOLD                 consumers
 trips/drivers CSV ─batch─┐                                   ┌─ zone_hourly_demand ─┐
 GPS ─Kafka─stream────────┼─► append-only ─gate─► conformed ──┤  driver_daily        ├─► BI star schema
                          │   (Delta,       (GX  (Delta,       │                      │   (dashboard)
                          │    lineage)      +    constraints, └─ trip_features ──────┼─► AI feature svc
                          │                 quar) merge, TT)      (point-in-time)      │   (offline+online)
   orchestrated by ONE idempotent DAG:  land >> gate >> silver >> [gold...] >> maintain
   observability: freshness · volume · drift   |   governance: PII class · access · PDPL retention

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
1. Git repository URL with full history and a one-command make pipeline (or DAG trigger).
  2. A runnable Mini-Lakehouse producing all bronze/silver/gold tables with documented grains/contracts.
  3. BENCHMARKS.md with the course benchmark tables filled from your runs (scan/cost, small-files, streaming dedup, serving latency).
  4. GOVERNANCE.md: PII classification, access levels, retention policy with PDPL justification, and a demonstrated erasure.
  5. 6-minute demo: one-command pipeline run, a streaming kill/restart (no dupes), a quality-gate quarantine, a time-travel audit, and the AI + BI consumers reading gold.
  6. DECISIONS.md: five one-paragraph engineering decisions with rationale (e.g., partition key choice, VACUUM retention, stream vs batch boundary, online store yes/no, feature window).

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text: Milestone Due Gate M-A: bronze landing (batch+stream) + profiling End Day 2 instructor spot-check M-B: ELT silver + Delta constraints + tests End Day 3 dbt test green + constrained Delta M-C: streaming exactly-once + quality gate + governance End Day 4 kill/restart + quarantine demo M-D: orchestrated DAG + gold + serving Day 5 H2–H3 one-command run + idempotent recovery M-E: demo + submission Day 5 H5 rubric scoring

docs.title: Grading Rubric (100 points)
docs.text:
Criterion Weight 90–100% band 70–89% band < 70% band Architecture & medallion contracts 15 Clean bronze/silver/gold, contracts documented + enforced, no bypass Minor contract gap or one bypass Layers muddled, gold from bronze, no contracts ELT & incrementality 15 Incremental merge + lookback; ≥ 6 tests; backfill proven Incremental works; thin tests or shaky backfill Full-refresh only; late-arrival bug; no tests Delta Lake mastery 15 Constraints, idempotent MERGE, time travel, justified VACUUM, erasure Most present; retention/erasure thin No constraints, non-idempotent, VACUUM misused Streaming 15 Exactly-once proven (kill/restart), watermark, checkpoint discipline Streams but dedup/watermark weak Duplicates on restart; processing-time aggregation Quality, observability, governance 15 Gate acts (fail-fast+quarantine), obs signals fire, PII+PDPL retention Some gaps (alert-only, partial obs) Alerts only; no quarantine; raw PII kept forever Orchestration & recovery 15 One-command idempotent DAG; clean failure recovery Runs but recovery/idempotency partial Hand-run steps; non-idempotent; no recovery Serving (AI + BI) & demo 10 PIT-correct features, offline==online, conformed BI, PDPL-safe; crisp demo Works; leakage or reconciliation thin Leakage; online≠offline; raw PII served

Pass ≥ 70. Distinction ≥ 90. Extensions add up to +5 bonus (capped at 100) only if mandatory scope is ≥ 80.

docs.title: Assessment Criteria Notes for Instructors
docs.text:
• Grade from the running platform and repository evidence first (one-command run, DAG recovery, data docs, benchmarks), demo second — the point of the course is that the platform speaks.
  • Anti-pattern flags that cap a criterion at 70%: feature leakage; non-idempotent gold; VACUUM RETAIN 0; alert-only quality gate; raw rider IDs in BI outputs; streaming without a dedicated checkpoint.
  • Verify one claim live: ask the participant to kill the stream and restart it and show zero duplicates, or to run the leakage drill and explain the inflated metric.

docs.title: Bonus Tasks (for early finishers / distinction seekers)
docs.text:
1. Wire an offline/online consistency test into CI and show it fail on an injected divergence.
  2. Add a Trino/Databricks-SQL direct-serve path and benchmark it against the materialised mart.
  3. Implement a data-contract test that fails the DAG when a gold grain is violated.
  4. Add multi-city 7-day backfill and prove idempotent equivalence to incremental runs.

docs.title: Quiz Bank (20 questions — use 10 per cohort, 15 min, closed book)
docs.text: Q1. Which architecture combines lake economics with warehouse reliability? → Lakehouse. Q2. What single property turns Parquet files into a Delta table? → the _delta_log transaction log. Q3. In a decoupled platform, which cost axis is usually the controllable lever? → compute (elastic), not storage. Q4. Two Parquet features that make remote reads cheap? → column pruning; row-group min/max stats (data skipping). Q5. Why did ELT win on the cloud over ETL? → cheap storage keeps raw; elastic compute transforms in-platform (reprocessable, auditable). Q6. What bug does a lookback window fix in an incremental model? → late-arriving data missed by a date = today filter. Q7. Why is MERGE-on-key idempotent but INSERT is not? → re-applying matched rows updates nothing; INSERT duplicates. Q8. Which ACID property does Delta snapshot isolation provide? → Isolation (readers see a consistent version). Q9. What does VACUUM trade away to reclaim storage? → time-travel history beyond the retention window. Q10. Why is partitioning by trip_id a mistake? → millions of tiny files (the small-files problem). Q11. Which two mechanisms give Structured Streaming + Delta exactly-once? → checkpointed Kafka offsets + Delta atomic per-batch commit. Q12. Event time vs processing time — which must windowed aggregations use, and why? → event time, so late events count in the right window. Q13. What does a streaming watermark bound? → how long late data is awaited / state kept before finalising a window. Q14. Where in the medallion should the quality gate run? → at promotion (bronze → silver). Q15. Give one failure warranting fail-fast and one warranting quarantine. → null/duplicate key (fail-fast); a few out-of-range values (quarantine). Q16. Name two observability signals that row-level checks miss. → freshness, volume (also distribution drift). Q17. Which PDPL principle argues against keeping precise GPS forever? → data minimisation / retention limits. Q18. What is feature leakage and why does it fool reviewers? → using info unavailable at prediction time; inflates offline metrics, fails live. Q19. How do you keep online and offline features consistent? → materialise/copy from the offline table; never re-implement. Q20. What makes numbers reconcile across dashboards? → conformed dimensions (one shared dim_date/dim_driver).

docs.title: Practical Assessments
docs.text:
PA-1 (30 min, Day 3): Given a Delta table VACUUMed with RETAIN 0 and a non-idempotent MERGE, restore correctness: fix retention, make the upsert idempotent, and prove time travel + a clean second run. Scored on diagnosis notes (40%), fixes (40%), verification evidence (20%).

PA-2 (30 min, Day 4): Given a streaming job with no checkpoint and a processing-time aggregation, produce exactly-once ingestion and an event-time windowed demand with a watermark; prove no duplicates on restart. Scored on correctness of fix (50%), evidence (30%), reasoning about semantics (20%).

PA-3: Capstone (rubric above) — 40% of course grade. Labs completion + PA-1/PA-2 — 60%.

docs.title: Evaluation Criteria Summary
docs.text:
Component Weight Evidence Lab completion (8 labs) 30% checkpoint commits + expected outputs PA-1 + PA-2 20% artefacts + notes Quiz 10% 10-question selection Capstone (Mini-Lakehouse) 40% rubric, platform-first

Badge issuance (Data-engineering badge) requires ≥ 70 overall and capstone ≥ 70 and zero academic-integrity flags (identical quarantine/benchmark artefacts across repos are checked) and no PDPL red flags (raw personal data served or retained beyond policy).

docs.text:

docs.title: Common Student Issues & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Frequency Resolution Java version / JAVA_HOME wrong for Spark High Pin Java 17; first-hour floater support; hosted-notebook fallback Delta extension not configured High Always use get_spark(); verify spark.sql.extensions Kafka container won't start / port clash High Pre-pull images; free 9092; provide a compose healthcheck Streaming duplicates on restart Medium One dedicated checkpointLocation per query (the M5 lesson) Small-files / slow reads after streaming Medium Scheduled OPTIMIZE; teach it as maintenance, not a fix dbt-spark connection/profile errors Medium Provide a working profiles.yml; run dbt debug first Feature leakage passes unnoticed Medium Make the leakage drill mandatory; add the leakage-lint bonus PySpark on Apple Silicon quirks Medium Use the provided arm64-compatible images; document JAVA_HOME Confusion between event vs processing time Medium Human-Kafka activity + the watermark clinic VACUUM removes nothing / RETAIN 0 blocked Low Explain the 7-day safety window; never disable in prod

docs.title: Timing Recommendations
docs.text:
• Protect Lab 4 (Delta) and Lab 5 (streaming) at full length; compress M2 theory (cost model lands through the lab) if behind.
  • If a cohort is strong: pull the offline/online CI check and multi-city backfill into main scope on Day 5.
  • If a cohort is weak: run the streaming exactly-once as a guided demo rather than a solo lab, but never skip the kill/restart observation — it is the module's thesis made visible.
  • Hard rule: the Mini-Lakehouse assembly (Day 5 H4) must start on time; cut discussion, not build time.
  • Reserve the leakage drill (M8) even if compressing — it is the single most memorable lesson and directly protects the capstone.

docs.title: Discussion Prompts (use during transitions)
docs.text:
1. "Your BI dashboard and your data scientist report different 'completed trips' numbers. Which architecture decision caused it, and which one fixes it?"
  2. "Storage is cheap and compute is elastic — so why did the migration bill go up? What discipline did they skip?"
  3. "A regulator asks what a table contained three weeks ago. Can your platform answer, and what must be true about VACUUM for it to?"
  4. "A model scores 0.95 offline. Are you excited or suspicious — and what do you check first?"
  5. "If the platform is the audit evidence and the morning decision, what does your current pipeline testify about your team's reliability?"

docs.title: Wrap-up (Day 5 final 15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Map each mandatory capstone requirement to the module that taught it (one slide): medallion (M1), economics (M2), ELT (M3), Delta (M4), streaming (M5), quality/governance (M6), orchestration (M7), serving (M8).
  • Forward pointer: SDA-DSC-215 (Big Data Analytics with Spark) scales exactly this Lakehouse to enterprise volumes with distributed execution, partitioning, and MLlib; SDA-DSC-313 builds advanced pipelines on this same substrate.
  • Collect: repo URLs, BENCHMARKS.md, GOVERNANCE.md, DECISIONS.md, and the mini_lakehouse/ folder; issue badge recommendations within 5 working days.

End of instructor package. All code samples target Python 3.11, Spark 3.5, Delta Lake 3.2, dbt 1.7+, Great Expectations 0.18+, and a single-broker Kafka. Verify pinned versions in the course lock file before each delivery. City names and business terms carry Arabic subtitles in slides; all code, table names, and identifiers remain in English per Saudi enterprise convention. PDPL obligations are treated as first-class constraints throughout.

docs.title: SDA-DSC-214 — Modern Data Engineering for AI Systems
هندسة البيانات الحديثة لأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي
docs.text:
Complete instructor-ready training package — SDAIA Academy, Capacity Building Sector.

Specialist level · 5 days × 5 learning hours = 25 hours · PySpark 3.5 · Delta Lake 3.2 · dbt 1.7 · Kafka · Great Expectations 0.18 · Redis.

Everything here is built around one evolving artefact: Masar (مسار), the national smart-mobility data platform of a Saudi ride-hailing and public-transit operator. There are no throwaway example datasets. Every lab produces a component of the Mini-Lakehouse capstone, so by Day 5 each participant owns a working, tested, governed Lakehouse feeding both an AI feature service and a BI dashboard.

The unifying question, repeated at every module boundary:

“What happens to Masar’s AI system if this part of the data platform fails?”

The design goal for this revision was to make the course less about learning five tools and more about engineering one trustworthy data product for AI.

docs.title: 1 · The slide deck
docs.text:
slides/SDA-DSC-214_Modern_Data_Engineering_for_AI_Systems.pptx — 105 slides, English, 16:9, speaker notes throughout.

Structure: course framing → Day 1 (M1 architecture evolution, M2 compute–storage economics) → Day 2 (M3 ETL vs ELT) → Day 3 (M4 Delta Lake and ACID) → Day 4 (M5 streaming, M6 quality, observability and governance) → the signature incident case study → Day 5 (M7 Mini-Lakehouse, M8 serving AI and BI) → capstone, rubric and instructor appendix.

The deck is rebuildable: cd slides && node build.js. Design system in lib.js, slide constructors in kit.js, content in c0_intro.js … c7_close.js. Edit content, rebuild, and the layout engine re-fits every text block automatically.

docs.title: 2 · Labs and activities
docs.text:
Lab Title Day LAB_00 Environment setup (send T-minus 2 days) before LAB_01 Land the Masar raw feeds into bronze 1 LAB_02 Cost and elasticity model 1 LAB_03 ELT pipeline to silver.trips 2 LAB_04 Delta: ACID, MERGE, time travel, maintenance 3 LAB_05 Stream GPS into the Lakehouse (exactly-once) 4 LAB_06 Quality gate and governance 4 LAB_07 Assemble and orchestrate the Mini-Lakehouse 5 LAB_08 Serve gold to AI and BI + the leakage drill 5

Each participant guide is standalone: header table, why-it-matters, exact setup commands, timed steps with full runnable code, expected console transcripts, acceptance checkboxes, self-check questions with hidden answers, an extended troubleshooting table, stretch goals, and the capstone requirement it satisfies. Each solution guide adds reference code, timed teaching moments, common wrong answers and how to redirect, minute-by-minute checkpoints, the filled benchmark table, and grading notes.

Three case studies were added specifically for this revision:

  • CS-09 — Databricks medallion architecture. Medallion as progressive refinement, anchored on the instructor question “Masar receives 15 million GPS events daily — which transformations belong in Bronze, Silver and Gold, and which must never occur before Bronze persistence?” Deliverable: a one-page Architecture Decision Record. Includes a 20-transformation classification table, a filled exemplar ADR and a blank template.
  • CS-10 — LinkedIn and Kafka. Kafka's origin as a central messaging backbone, turned into a scored design exercise rather than a tool tutorial: Vehicles → Kafka → Structured Streaming → bronze.gps_events → silver.vehicle_positions → fan-out to ETA features and operations alerts, with three escalating rounds (late events, duplicates, out-of-order timestamps).
  • CS-11 — The Masar National Mobility Data Incident. The signature case study of the course. At 08:00 demand-forecasting accuracy drops 18% while the BI dashboard looks entirely normal. Teams investigate a six-stage evidence pack and reconstruct the chain: GPS producer 2.4.0 → 2.5.0 silently changes speed_kmh to metres per second → schema validation passes because the type is unchanged → Silver continues → rolling_avg_speed_10m is corrupted → the ETA feature distribution shifts → the model degrades, invisibly to BI. Includes the remediation exercise, a blameless post-incident review template, and the facilitator answer key with the exact detection queries.

ACT-09 — feature validity classification is the client-requested activity that connects data engineering directly to production AI reliability: every column of gold.eta_features is classified as VALID / STALE / LEAKAGE / UNAVAILABLE ONLINE against the single question “could this feature have been known at prediction time?” It also appears as the mandatory drill in LAB_08 and as practical assessment PA-3.

The incident fixture is the one to know about: incident_speed_unit/gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson, 47,583 events at producer_version 2.5.0 whose mean speed_kmh is 3.60× lower than the 2.4.0 population in the same hour — schema-identical, semantically wrong.

It is the dataset behind the DataTalksClub Data Engineering Zoomcamp precisely because it is large, messy, has anomalies, requires cleaning, and has had genuine schema changes over time. data/raw/trips_YYYY-MM-DD.csv (CSV, header, ~48,200 rows/day): trip_id, rider_id, driver_id, vehicle_id, city, pickup_zone_id, dropoff_zone_id, pickup_ts, dropoff_ts, distance_km, duration_min, fare_sar, surge_multiplier, payment_type, status, dropoff_geohash - Deliberate defects: 3.1% null dropoff_geohash; mixed timestamp formats in ~2% of rows (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS vs DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM); a few negative duration_min; duplicate trip_id across the late-arrival fixture; status in {completed, cancelled_rider, cancelled_driver, no_show}.

docs.title: GPS is gzipped
docs.text:
The shipped GPS files are gps_YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson.gz, not .ndjson. Five days of raw NDJSON would be 220 MB; gzipped it is 26 MB, which keeps the whole package inside the 40 MB repo budget. Nothing else is compressed.

Every tool in this package reads either form transparently. In your own code:

import gzip, json
opener = gzip.open if path.endswith(".gz") else open
with opener(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in fh]

# Spark reads gzipped NDJSON natively — the codec is inferred from the extension.
spark.read.json("data/raw/gps/*.ndjson.gz")      # works
spark.read.json("data/raw/gps/")                 # also works: mixed .ndjson / .ndjson.gz

# pandas, likewise
pd.read_json(path, lines=True, compression="infer")

Gzip is not splittable, so one file is one Spark task. At the shipped scale that is irrelevant (5 MB per file); at full scale, regenerate without --gzip-gps — which is the default — and you get plain, splittable NDJSON.

docs.title: Regenerating
docs.text:
Everything is seeded. Same seed + same arguments ⇒ byte-identical output, on any machine with Python 3.11 and no third-party packages.

cd data/generators

# the shipped sample, exactly as committed
python3 generate_masar.py --start 2026-06-01 --days 5 --out ../raw --scale 0.15 --gzip-gps
python3 inject_defects.py --raw ../raw --out ../fixtures --start 2026-06-01 --days 5

# FULL SCALE — the 30-day dataset the lab specs describe (~9 GB, ~7 minutes)
python3 generate_masar.py --start 2026-06-01 --days 30 --out ../raw --scale 1.0

# full scale but compressed (~1.3 GB) if disk is tight
python3 generate_masar.py --start 2026-06-01 --days 30 --out ../raw --scale 1.0 --gzip-gps

# a clean copy with EVERY deliberate defect switched off (useful as a control)
python3 generate_masar.py --days 5 --out ../raw_clean --scale 0.15 --clean

Dependencies: Python 3.11 standard library only. No Faker, no numpy required (verify_sample.py uses pandas for the profile pass; the manifest pass is stdlib-only).

docs.title: Size and scale table
docs.text:
Per day, and for the 30-day window the course assumes:

--scale trips/day GPS pings/day trips CSV/day GPS NDJSON/day GPS .gz/day 30 days, plain 30 days, --gzip-gps 0.02 964 ~23,300 149 KB 5.9 MB 0.7 MB ~200 MB ~30 MB 0.15 (shipped) 7,230 ~175,000 1.1 MB 44 MB 5.1 MB ~1.4 GB ~200 MB 0.50 24,100 ~581,000 3.7 MB 147 MB 17 MB ~4.6 GB ~680 MB 1.00 (lab spec) 48,200 ~1,161,000 7.3 MB 295 MB 34 MB ~9.0 GB ~1.3 GB

Fixed-size files regardless of scale: drivers.csv 3,450 rows / 406 KB, vehicles.csv 3,864 rows / 286 KB, zones.csv 48 rows / 3 KB. weather_hourly.csv is 72 rows/day. payments_*.csv follows trips (~96% of trips generate a payment row).

Generation runs at roughly 14 seconds per full-scale day on a lab laptop, single-threaded.

docs.title: Verifying a regeneration
docs.text:
raw/_MANIFEST.json records, for every file: relative path, row count, byte size, sha256, plus the seed and every argument used. That is what makes a regeneration checkable rather than merely plausible.

cd data/generators

# stdlib only: recompute every sha256 and compare
python3 verify_sample.py --manifest-only

# plus a full profile: row counts, null rates, duplicate counts, observed defect rates
python3 verify_sample.py

Exit code 0 means every file matched and every observed defect rate is within 25% of the documented rate. Anything else prints exactly which file or which rate drifted.

To prove a fresh regeneration reproduces the shipped data byte-for-byte:

python3 generate_masar.py --start 2026-06-01 --days 5 --out /tmp/check --scale 0.15 --gzip-gps
diff <(jq -S '.files' ../raw/_MANIFEST.json) <(jq -S '.files' /tmp/check/_MANIFEST.json) && echo IDENTICAL

(generated_at_utc is the only field that legitimately differs between runs.)

docs.title: The deliberate defects
docs.text:
raw/ is not clean, on purpose. These are the background defects — the everyday mess a real feed carries. They are all documented, all controlled by a CLI flag, and all ON by default. --clean turns every one of them off.

defect flag documented rate observed in the shipped sample trips.dropoff_geohash NULL (injected, of completed rows) --null-geohash-rate 3.100% 3.081% trips mixed timestamp format (DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM) --mixed-ts-rate 2.000% 2.017% trips.duration_min negative --negative-duration-per-day ~12/day @ scale 1.0 15 rows (3/day at scale 0.15) gps duplicate event_id --gps-dup-rate 0.400% 0.398% gps out-of-order ts --gps-ooo-rate 1.000% 1.001% drivers.hire_date in three formats --no-hire-date-formats 3 formats 3 (YYYY-MM-DD 2,137 · DD/MM/YYYY 835 · Mon DD, YYYY 478)

docs.title: One number that needs explaining: dropoff_geohash
docs.text:
The observed overall null rate of dropoff_geohash in raw/ is 9.840%, not 3.1%. That is correct and it is two different things added together:

  • 3.081% of completed trips have an injected NULL geohash. This is the deliberate defect the lab specs name.
  • 6.974% of all trips are cancelled_rider / cancelled_driver / no_show. Those rows have no dropoff at all, so dropoff_ts, distance_km, duration_min and dropoff_geohash are structurally NULL. This is not a defect; it is what the data means.

Profiling bronze naively and reporting "9.8% nulls" is itself a teaching moment: a null rate without a WHERE status = 'completed' predicate is a number about the schema, not about quality. Both figures are printed by the generator and by verify_sample.py, and both are recorded in _MANIFEST.json.

The fixtures under fixtures/ are a different category: staged, isolated incidents rather than background noise. Each has its own README with the exact detection signal.

docs.title: The signature incident
docs.text:
fixtures/incident_speed_unit/gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson.gz is the one to read first.

A device-firmware rollout moves 34% of the fleet to producer_version 2.5.0. The payload keeps the field name speed_kmh and its double type — and starts writing metres per second. Schema validation passes. Range checks pass. Freshness, volume and row counts are all normal. No error is raised anywhere.

gold.eta_features.rolling_avg_speed_10m silently falls by 3.6× for a third of the fleet, the ETA model starts over-predicting journey times, and nobody connects it to a line in a device changelog.

Verified in the shipped sample: for the same 47,583 events, mean speed_kmh is 35.45 before the unit change and 9.85 as shipped — exactly 3.60×, the m/s → km/h factor. Compared against the whole raw day (mean 33.63 km/h across all vehicles and hours) the observed ratio is 3.41×; the gap is not an error, it is the incident being scoped to afternoon and evening hours, when speeds are genuinely lower. Segmenting drift by producer_version removes that confound — which is precisely why you must segment.

That is the course's unifying question made concrete:

"What happens to Masar's AI system if THIS part of the data platform fails?"

Here, nothing failed. Every component did exactly what it was told. Type-compatibility is not semantic compatibility.

docs.title: Streaming the GPS feed (Module 5)
docs.text:
cd data/generators

# 500 events/s, one hour of event time per minute, to Kafka topic masar.gps.raw
python3 emit_gps_stream.py --date 2026-06-01 --rate 500 --speedup 60

# with live faults
python3 emit_gps_stream.py --date 2026-06-05 --inject late,dupes,unit-shift

# no broker? it degrades to NDJSON and says so — the lab is not blocked
python3 emit_gps_stream.py --date 2026-06-01 --sink file --out ./replay.ndjson

Needs kafka-python for the Kafka path (pip install kafka-python). Messages are keyed by vehicle_id so a vehicle's pings stay in one partition and per-vehicle ordering survives — Lab 5 asks participants to justify that choice against keying by trip_id.

docs.title: Optional: the NYC TLC benchmark
docs.text:
python3 generators/nyc_tlc_prep.py --month 2024-01 --out ../raw_nyc

Downloads a month of NYC TLC yellow-taxi Parquet from the official CloudFront endpoint (https://d37ci6vzurychx.cloudfront.net/trip-data/yellow_tripdata_{YYYY}-{MM}.parquet) and maps it onto the Masar trips schema.

This is the dataset the DataTalksClub Data Engineering Zoomcamp is built on, and it earns that place: it is large (~3M rows/month, ~40 GB across the history), genuinely messy (negative total_amount, zero-distance trips, timestamps outside their own file's month), and it has had real schema changes — precise coordinates removed in 2016-07 and replaced by PULocationID/DOLocationID, congestion_surcharge and airport_fee added mid-stream, and CSV → Parquet with type changes in 2022-05.

No lab depends on it. With no internet the script prints the exact URL, where to save the file, and the one-line curl to fetch it elsewhere — then exits cleanly.

docs.title: Licence and provenance
docs.text:
Fully synthetic. No real personal data. No real trips, riders, drivers, vehicles or plates.

  • Every rider_id, driver_id, vehicle_id and trip_id is generated from a seeded PRNG.
  • Driver names are assembled from a small internal pool of common Saudi given and family names. Any resemblance to a real individual is coincidental and statistically inevitable given the pool size — these are not records about anyone.
  • national_id_hash, phone_hash and plate_hash are SHA-256 digests of synthetic strings. There is no underlying real identifier, and nothing to reverse.
  • GPS coordinates are jittered around published district centroids. They describe no person's movements.
  • Zone names, districts and approximate centroids are real public geography (Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam) — public reference data, not personal data.
  • Currency is SAR; the fare model is invented and does not represent any operator's tariff.

The dataset is nonetheless treated as if it were personal data throughout the course. That is the point: rider_id and precise GPS are classified, minimised, retained and erased under Saudi PDPL rules in every lab. See DATA_DICTIONARY.md for the per-column classification and retention policy.

The optional NYC TLC data is not synthetic: it is public trip-record data published by the New York City Taxi & Limousine Commission, containing no rider identifiers and (since 2016-07) no precise coordinates. If you publish anything derived from it, cite https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page.

Course material: SDAIA Academy, SDA-DSC-214. Internal training use.

docs.title: Masar data dictionary — SDA-DSC-214
docs.text: Canonical column definitions for every file in data/raw/ and data/fixtures/. Schemas here are authoritative and match CONVENTIONS.md. Do not add, rename or reorder columns; downstream labs, dbt models, Great Expectations suites and the capstone all bind to these names.

docs.title: How to read the PDPL column
docs.text:
Every column carries a classification under the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law. The four levels used across this course:

class meaning default control public reference data with no link to an individual no restriction internal operational data, commercially sensitive, not personal role-based read personal identifies or relates to an identifiable natural person column-level access control; never in BI or the online store in raw form; in scope for erasure sensitive-personal personal data whose exposure creates concrete risk to the individual — here, precise location and identity hashes strict need-to-know; minimise (geohash, not lat/lon); shortest retention; in scope for erasure

Retention is the maximum period the raw value may be kept in the lakehouse before the retention job deletes it and VACUUM makes the deletion physical. Aggressive retention protects data subjects and cuts storage; conservative retention preserves the audit trail. The tension is the point — the numbers below are the course's documented, defensible policy, not a universal answer.

Timezone: every timestamp is stored in UTC. The business operates in Asia/Riyadh (UTC+3). Presentation converts; storage never does. Roughly 2% of trips timestamps are deliberately written as DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM instead of YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS — see README.md#the-deliberate-defects.

Currency: SAR throughout.

docs.title: raw/trips_YYYY-MM-DD.csv
docs.text:
One row per trip request. ~48,200 rows/day at --scale 1.0; 7,230/day in the shipped sample. CSV, header row, UTF-8, , separated, " quoted where needed.

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention trip_id string no TRP-20260601-0000000 Primary key. TRP-<YYYYMMDD>-<7-digit sequence>. Unique within the raw feed; the fixtures deliberately break that. internal 7 years (financial record) rider_id string no RDR-013698 Pseudonymous rider identifier. The subject key for PDPL erasure. Never emit raw into BI or the Redis online store. personal 24 months, or on erasure request driver_id string no DRV-02492 FK → drivers.driver_id. Identifies a natural person (a driver). personal 7 years (employment/tax) vehicle_id string no VEH-00884 FK → vehicles.vehicle_id. internal 7 years city string no DMM City code, one of RUH (Riyadh), JED (Jeddah), DMM (Dammam). The dirty_batch fixture injects out-of-domain values. public indefinite pickup_zone_id string no Z-DMM-10 FK → zones.zone_id. Where the trip started. internal 24 months dropoff_zone_id string no Z-DMM-06 FK → zones.zone_id. Requested destination — populated even for cancelled trips. internal 24 months pickup_ts timestamp (UTC) no 2026-06-01 19:39:00 Trip start. ~2% of rows use DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM instead (deliberate). Combined with rider_id this is behavioural data. personal 24 months dropoff_ts timestamp (UTC) yes 2026-06-01 19:44:12 Trip end. NULL for cancelled_rider, cancelled_driver, no_show — structurally, not as a defect. personal 24 months distance_km double yes 3.04 Metered distance. NULL when the trip did not complete. internal 24 months duration_min double yes 5.2 Metered duration. NULL when the trip did not complete. A handful of rows per day are negative (deliberate defect). Never assume dropoff_ts - pickup_ts equals this. internal 24 months fare_sar double no 12.01 Total charged, SAR. 0.00 or a small cancellation fee for non-completed trips. Correlated with distance, duration and surge. The currency_shift fixture silently multiplies one city's values by 100. internal 7 years (financial record) surge_multiplier double no 1.0 Demand multiplier, 1.0–3.0 in 0.1 steps. Rises at the morning and evening peaks, on Fridays after Jumu'ah, in bad weather (dust, sandstorm, rain, fog) and at airport pickups. internal 7 years payment_type string no mada One of mada, credit_card, apple_pay, stc_pay, cash, wallet. mada is the Saudi national debit network. internal 7 years status string no completed One of completed (93.0%), cancelled_rider (4.2%), cancelled_driver (1.9%), no_show (0.9%). Everything except completed implies NULL dropoff fields. internal 7 years dropoff_geohash string yes thewke6 Precision-7 geohash (~150 m cell) of the dropoff point. This is minimised precise location — Masar deliberately stores a cell, not coordinates. NULL for non-completed trips (structural) and injected NULL on 3.1% of completed trips (deliberate defect). sensitive-personal 90 days at precision 7, then truncate to precision 5

Known correlations to preserve if you regenerate: fare_sar ~ distance_km r ≈ 0.94; fare_sar ~ duration_min r ≈ 0.98; mean implied speed drops from ~38 km/h at 03:00 local to ~21 km/h at 08:00 and 17:00–18:00 local; Friday's hourly demand curve is materially different from Sunday–Thursday's (late start, post-Jumu'ah bump, strong evening).

docs.title: raw/gps/gps_YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson[.gz]
docs.text:
Newline-delimited JSON, one object per GPS ping. ~25 pings per completed trip; ~1,161,000 rows/day at --scale 1.0, ~175,000/day in the shipped sample. Shipped gzipped — see README.md#gps-is-gzipped.

{"event_id":"ev_00009f025f480001","vehicle_id":"VEH-00884","driver_id":"DRV-02492",
 "trip_id":"TRP-20260601-0000000","ts":"2026-06-01T19:38:56Z",
 "payload":{"lat":26.41803,"lon":50.10770,"speed_kmh":15.3,"heading_deg":211,"accuracy_m":17.3},
 "producer_version":"2.4.0"}
field type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention event_id string no ev_00009f025f480001 Event key for exactly-once ingest and deduplication. ~0.4% are duplicated (deliberate defect) — the stream must dedupe on this. internal 30 days raw vehicle_id string no VEH-00884 FK → vehicles.vehicle_id. The Kafka message key — co-partitions a vehicle's pings so per-vehicle ordering survives. internal 30 days raw driver_id string no DRV-02492 FK → drivers.driver_id. Makes each ping attributable to a natural person. personal 30 days raw trip_id string no TRP-20260601-0000000 FK → trips.trip_id. The only path from a ping to a rider — an erasure that filters on rider_id alone misses GPS entirely. internal 30 days raw ts timestamp (UTC, RFC3339 Z) no 2026-06-01T19:38:56Z Event time, from the device — not ingest time. ~1% arrive out of order (deliberate defect); the late_pings fixture adds events that are minutes late. personal 30 days raw payload.lat double no 26.41803 Latitude, 5 dp (~1 m). Precise location. sensitive-personal 30 days, then aggregate to geohash-5 payload.lon double no 50.10770 Longitude, 5 dp. Precise location. sensitive-personal 30 days, then aggregate to geohash-5 payload.speed_kmh double no 15.3 Instantaneous speed in km/h — when producer_version is 2.4.0. Source of gold.eta_features.rolling_avg_speed_10m. See the warning below. internal 30 days raw payload.heading_deg int no 211 Compass heading, 0–359. internal 30 days raw payload.accuracy_m double no 17.3 Reported GPS accuracy radius in metres, ~3–18. internal 30 days raw producer_version string no 2.4.0 Device firmware version. Always carry this into bronze and always segment drift checks by it — without it, the signature incident is undiagnosable. internal keep with the row

docs.title: ⚠ speed_kmh is not always km/h
docs.text:
producer_version 2.4.0 emits speed_kmh in kilometres per hour. producer_version 2.5.0 emits the same field name, same double type — in metres per second. This is the course's signature incident (fixtures/incident_speed_unit/). Schema validation, range checks, freshness, volume and row counts all pass. Only a distribution check segmented by producer_version, or a cross-field reconciliation against distance_km / duration_min from trips, catches it.

Any model or feature reading speed_kmh must either filter on producer_version or normalise: speed_kmh_true = speed_kmh * 3.6 if producer_version >= "2.5.0" else speed_kmh.

docs.title: raw/drivers.csv
docs.text:
Driver dimension. 3,450 rows, fixed — not affected by --scale.

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention driver_id string no DRV-00001 Primary key. personal 7 years after termination full_name_en string no Sara Al Shehri Driver's name, Latin transliteration. Synthetic, from an internal name pool. personal 7 years after termination city string no RUH Home city, one of RUH, JED, DMM. internal 7 years hire_date string (three formats) no Jul 22, 2019 Deliberately inconsistent. Approximately: YYYY-MM-DD 62%, DD/MM/YYYY 24%, Mon DD, YYYY 14%. Cast it in staging (stg_drivers) or every date filter downstream is wrong. internal 7 years rating double no 4.78 Rolling rider rating, 3.2–5.0, mean ≈ 4.72. A performance measure about a natural person. personal 24 months status string no active One of active (90%), inactive (8.5%), suspended (1.5%). personal 7 years national_id_hash string (hex, 32) no 8629a325a33df68a… SHA-256 digest (truncated) of a synthetic national-ID string. A pseudonymised national identifier is still personal data under PDPL, and re-identifiable in combination — treat it as sensitive and never join it into a shared mart. sensitive-personal 7 years, strict access phone_hash string (hex, 32) no 6958c7fe7046e5d2… SHA-256 digest of a synthetic phone number. Same reasoning. sensitive-personal 24 months, strict access

docs.title: raw/vehicles.csv
docs.text:
Vehicle dimension. 3,864 rows (one per driver plus ~12% spare fleet).

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention vehicle_id string no VEH-00001 Primary key. internal 7 years plate_hash string (hex, 32) no fde902de0dae2702… SHA-256 digest of a synthetic plate string. A plate identifies a vehicle, and through the fleet roster a person — pseudonymised, not anonymised. personal 7 years, restricted make string no Chevrolet Manufacturer. public indefinite model string no Malibu Model. public indefinite model_year int no 2023 2018–2026, skewed toward recent years. public indefinite capacity int no 4 Passenger seats: 4 (saloon), 7 (SUV), 11 (van). public indefinite fuel_type string no petrol One of petrol, diesel, hybrid, electric. Feeds the fleet-emissions angle in the capstone. public indefinite city string no RUH Registered operating city. internal 7 years

docs.title: raw/zones.csv
docs.text:
Zone dimension: 48 rows over three cities. Real district geography, Arabic and English.

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention zone_id string no Z-RUH-01 Primary key, Z-<CITY>-<NN>. public indefinite zone_name_en string no Olaya District name, English. public indefinite zone_name_ar string no العليا District name, Arabic. UTF-8. Keep the encoding end to end — a mojibake'd Arabic label is a real, common ingestion bug. public indefinite city string no RUH RUH (21 zones), JED (15), DMM (12). public indefinite district string no Olaya Municipal district grouping. public indefinite centroid_lat double no 24.6908 Zone centroid latitude. Reference geography, not a person's location. public indefinite centroid_lon double no 46.6853 Zone centroid longitude. public indefinite

Zone-to-zone flows are strongly non-uniform by design (gravity model with airport, commute and retail boosts): the busiest pair carries ~500 trips over the shipped 5 days against a median of 24. Uniform flows would make partition-skew and data-skipping lessons meaningless.

docs.title: raw/payments_YYYY-MM-DD.csv
docs.text:
One row per trip that generated a charge (~96% of trips).

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention payment_id string no PAY-20260601-0000000 Primary key. internal 7 years trip_id string no TRP-20260601-0000000 FK → trips.trip_id. Every row references a real trip in the same day's file. internal 7 years amount_sar double no 12.01 Amount charged, SAR. Must reconcile with trips.fare_sar — that reconciliation is a Module 6 quality check. internal 7 years (financial record) method string no mada Same domain as trips.payment_type. internal 7 years status string no settled settled (~95.5%), pending (~2.8%), failed (~1.1%), refunded (~0.6%). internal 7 years settled_ts timestamp (UTC) no 2026-06-01 20:08:15 When the payment settled. Can fall on the day after the trip — this is the mechanism behind late-arriving trips and the reason silver.trips needs a lookback window. internal 7 years

docs.title: raw/weather_hourly.csv
docs.text:
Hourly weather per city. 72 rows/day (3 cities × 24 hours), independent of --scale.

column type nullable example business meaning PDPL retention city string no DMM RUH, JED, DMM. public indefinite hour_ts timestamp (UTC) no 2026-05-31 21:00:00 Hour bucket, UTC. Note that 2026-05-31 21:00:00Z is local midnight on 2026-06-01 — the file starts three hours before the first local day, which is exactly the timezone trap Module 3 drills. public indefinite temp_c double no 30.0 Temperature, °C. Peaks ~15:00 local, troughs ~05:00 local; clamped to a plausible KSA June envelope of 20–48. Observed in the shipped sample: 22.2–48.0. public indefinite condition string no clear One of clear, cloudy, haze, dust, sandstorm, rain, fog. Conditions persist for several hours (weather states, not per-hour dice), so a dust event lasts a shift, not an hour. Drives surge (up to +0.42 in a sandstorm) and reduces speed (down to ×0.74). Feeds gold.eta_features.weather_condition. The shipped 5-day sample contains clear 207h, dust 67h, cloudy 48h, haze 34h, rain 4h — sandstorm and fog are rare enough that a 5-day window may not contain one; regenerate more days if a lab needs them. public indefinite visibility_km double no 10.0 Visibility, 0.2–10.0 km. Falls sharply in sandstorm and fog. Observed in the shipped sample: 1.9–10.0. public indefinite

docs.title: raw/_MANIFEST.json
docs.text:
Not a data file — the reproducibility record. Top-level keys:

key meaning seed, args everything needed to reproduce the run exactly generator_version bump this if the generator's output changes semantically files[] per file: path, kind, rows, bytes, sha256 documented_defect_rates the rates the labs are written against observed_defect_counts what this particular run actually produced timezone, currency, synthetic, personal_data provenance

generators/verify_sample.py compares a directory against this file. See README.md#verifying-a-regeneration.

docs.title: fixtures/
docs.text:
Each fixture reuses the schema of the file it derives from, so no new dictionary entries are needed. Full detail, including the expected detection signal, is in each folder's README.md.

fixture schema lab what is wrong corrections/trips_corrections_2026-06-03.csv trips 4 4 rows that must UPDATE, 1 that must INSERT — the MERGE idempotency drill late_trips/trips_late_2026-06-02.csv trips 3 120 never-seen trips arriving 2 days late + 6 identical re-sends late_pings/gps_late_2026-06-04.ndjson gps_events + _note_delay_seconds 5 520 shuffled, late events straddling a 3-minute watermark dirty_batch/trips_2026-06-05_dirty.csv trips 6 40 null keys, 8 duplicate keys, 120 out-of-range fares, 25 bad city codes, 15 reversed timestamps currency_shift/trips_2026-06-05_currency_shift.csv trips 6 JED fares ×100 (SAR → halalas), every row individually valid erasure_request/pdpl_erasure_2026-06-10.json request document 4 7 rider_ids to erase, 29 rows in the shipped sample incident_speed_unit/gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson.gz gps_events 5 / 6 / 8 producer_version 2.5.0, speed_kmh carrying m/s

late_pings/*.ndjson carries one extra key, _note_delay_seconds, stating how late each event is. It is instructional metadata, not part of the contract — strip it before producing to Kafka (emit_gps_stream.py does this automatically).

docs.title: Medallion columns added downstream
docs.text:
Not present in raw/ — added by the ingest layer and listed here so the contract is complete.

column added at type meaning _ingested_at bronze timestamp Processing time — when the row landed. Never confuse with pickup_ts / ts (event time). _source_file bronze string The file this row came from. The first thing you need in an incident. _batch_id bronze string Ingest run identifier; makes a batch retractable.

CONVENTIONS.md defines the bronze, silver and gold table names these feed.

docs.title: Masar teaching fixtures — SDA-DSC-214
docs.text:
These are staged incidents, not background noise. ../raw/ already carries realistic low-level defects (null geohashes, mixed date formats, a few duplicate GPS events). The folders here each isolate one failure mode so a lab can detect it, decide on it, and prove the fix.

folder file lab the failure corrections/ trips_corrections_2026-06-03.csv Lab 4 corrections applied by append instead of MERGE late_trips/ trips_late_2026-06-02.csv Lab 3 late-arriving data missed by date = today late_pings/ gps_late_2026-06-04.ndjson Lab 5 late + out-of-order events vs the watermark dirty_batch/ trips_2026-06-05_dirty.csv Lab 6 fail-fast (integrity) vs quarantine (partial) currency_shift/ trips_2026-06-05_currency_shift.csv Lab 6 a ×100 unit change every row-level check passes erasure_request/ pdpl_erasure_2026-06-10.json Lab 4 PDPL erasure, time travel, and VACUUM incident_speed_unit/ gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson Lab 5/6/8 the signature incident — speed_kmh carrying m/s

Every folder has its own README.md with the exact expected detection signal and the numbers to check against.

Regenerate all of them with:

cd generators
python3 inject_defects.py --raw ../raw --out ../fixtures

All content is fully synthetic and derived from ../raw.

docs.title: Fixture — corrections/
docs.text: File: trips_corrections_2026-06-03.csv (5 rows, canonical trips schema) Used by: Lab 4 (Delta Lake and ACID) — MERGE / upsert idempotency drill. Also referenced by: Module 4 instructor demo ("upsert twice, second run updates 0 rows").

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
A batch of re-scored trips issued by Masar's support and pricing team two days after 2026-06-03 settled. It is not corrupt data — it is a legitimate correction feed, and it is the reason silver.trips must be an idempotent MERGE on trip_id rather than an append.

trip_id correction TRP-20260603-0002298 surge dispute upheld, 50.65 -> 46.05 SAR TRP-20260603-0005907 GPS route re-snapped, 8.11 -> 6.33 km, fare re-scored TRP-20260603-0003717 reclassified completed -> no_show, cancellation fee only TRP-20260603-0002801 payment_type corrected to credit_card TRP-20260603-9000001 previously missing trip, must INSERT (not update)

Four rows match an existing trip_id in bronze.trips / silver.trips for 2026-06-03 and must UPDATE. One row (TRP-20260603-9000001) does not exist upstream and must INSERT — so a WHEN MATCHED -only MERGE silently loses it.

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
• First MERGE run: 4 rows updated, 1 row inserted.
  • Second MERGE run with the same file: 0 updated, 0 inserted — this is the idempotency proof. If the second run reports non-zero, the merge condition is not on the true key.
  • DESCRIBE HISTORY silver.trips shows two commits; VERSION AS OF the first reproduces the pre-correction fares.
  • A naive INSERT INTO instead of MERGE shows up as duplicate trip_ids — the dbt unique test on trip_id fails.

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: "What happens to Masar's AI system if this part of the platform fails?" Corrections applied by append double-count revenue and feed the ETA model two contradictory labels for the same trip.

docs.title: Fixture — currency_shift/
docs.text: File: trips_2026-06-05_currency_shift.csv (7230 rows, canonical trips schema) Used by: Lab 6 (Data Quality and Observability) — distribution-drift detection. Case study: "The Silent Currency Bug at Muqeem Analytics" (Module 6).

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
An upstream fare service was redeployed and, for JED only, started reporting fare_sar in halalas instead of riyals — a silent ×100 unit change. Every row is still a valid row. Nothing about the schema changed. No key is null. No value is negative.

metric value rows in file 7230 rows affected (city = 'JED') 2125 other cities untouched — this is scoped drift, not a whole-batch failure mean fare_sar, JED, baseline day 2026-06-03 34.39 mean fare_sar, JED, this file before the shift 37.40 mean fare_sar, JED, this file as shipped 3739.86

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
• Row-level checks pass. expect_column_values_to_be_between("fare_sar", 0, 100000) is satisfied; so is every not-null, uniqueness and type check. That is the lesson.
  • A per-city mean-fare drift check against a frozen baseline fires: JED mean moves from ~34 SAR to ~3740 SAR — roughly 100×, far outside any sane tolerance (e.g. ±25% or a 3σ / PSI > 0.25 threshold).
  • RUH and DMM do not drift, which is what tells you the cause is source-scoped, not a platform-wide bug — and points the investigation straight at the JED vendor feed.

Baseline hygiene: freeze the baseline on a known-good window (2026-06-03, before the deployment). If you compute the baseline after ingesting this batch you "baseline the bug" and the check never fires again — that is the sim-baselinebug simulation in Module 6.

docs.title: Correct response
docs.text:
1. Quarantine JED only — do not block RUH and DMM; they are fine.
  2. Alert with the evidence (baseline mean, observed mean, ratio, affected city).
  3. Correct with a MERGE (Module 4) once the unit is normalised — bronze stays immutable, silver is repaired, and DESCRIBE HISTORY records who fixed what.
  4. Record lineage from silver.trips back to the vendor feed so the next redeployment is caught in a day, not a fortnight.

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: Schema validation is type-checking, not meaning-checking. A double that is 100× wrong is still a double. Only a distribution check compares the data to what the business expects, and only a frozen baseline gives it something honest to compare to.

docs.title: Fixture — dirty_batch/
docs.text: File: trips_2026-06-05_dirty.csv (7238 rows, canonical trips schema) Used by: Lab 6 (Data Quality, Observability, Governance) — the fail-fast vs quarantine decision.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
One day's trips (2026-06-05) with a mixed bag of injected faults. The mix is the whole point: a mature quality gate does not apply one policy to everything.

class fault rows correct gate action Integrity trip_id is NULL 20 fail-fast — block the batch Integrity rider_id is NULL 20 fail-fast — block the batch Integrity duplicate trip_id 8 fail-fast — block the batch Range fare_sar negative 40 quarantine the rows, promote the rest Range fare_sar ~4200× too large 40 quarantine the rows, promote the rest Business rule fare_sar = 0 on a completed trip 40 quarantine the rows, promote the rest Domain city not in {RUH, JED, DMM} (RIYADH, ruh, DMM, XX, empty, …) 25 quarantine the rows, promote the rest Temporal dropoff_ts before pickup_ts 15 quarantine the rows, promote the rest — clean rows ~7030 promote to silver.trips

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
Run the Great Expectations suite quality/suites/silver_trips_suite.py against this file at the bronze → silver promotion point:

  1. expect_column_values_to_not_be_null("trip_id") → fails, unexpected_count = 20
  2. expect_column_values_to_be_unique("trip_id") → fails, unexpected_count = 8 → the gate blocks: 0 rows promoted, 0 quarantined, an alert is raised. This is the fail-fast branch: you cannot dedupe or repair a missing key, and a partially-keyed batch corrupts every downstream MERGE.
  3. Fix or drop the key faults, re-run. Now only partial expectations fail: expect_column_values_to_be_between("fare_sar", 0, 2000), expect_column_values_to_be_in_set("city", ["RUH","JED","DMM"]), and the pickup/dropoff ordering rule. → the gate quarantines ~160 rows into silver.trips_quarantine and promotes ~7030.

Benchmark table to fill in during the lab:

batch rows in promoted quarantined gate action clean (../../raw/trips_2026-06-05.csv) 0 promote dirty (this file) 7238 0 0 fail-fast (blocked) dirty, keys repaired 7230 ~7030 ~160 quarantine

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: A gate that only alerts is not a gate. If this batch is promoted with a warning, gold.fact_trip reports a negative revenue day, gold.eta_features trains on trips that ended before they started, and the city dimension grows four spellings of Riyadh.

docs.title: Fixture — erasure_request/
docs.text: File: pdpl_erasure_2026-06-10.json Used by: Lab 4 (Delta Lake and ACID) — the compliant-delete drill. Also referenced by: Module 6 PDPL clinic, Module 4 case study (reproduce a filing while honouring an erasure).

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
A data-subject erasure request under the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), naming 7 rider_ids that appear across the shipped sample. It is the input to the "right to be forgotten" exercise.

  • rider_ids in scope: RDR-006890, RDR-007660, RDR-009268, RDR-015753, RDR-016006, RDR-016557, RDR-017976
  • rows to delete from silver.trips in the shipped sample: 29
  • dates touched: 2026-06-01, 2026-06-02, 2026-06-03, 2026-06-04, 2026-06-05

All rider_ids are synthetic. No real person is represented.

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
-- before
SELECT count(*) FROM silver.trips WHERE rider_id IN (…);   -- 29

DELETE FROM silver.trips WHERE rider_id IN (…);            -- atomic, one commit

-- after
SELECT count(*) FROM silver.trips WHERE rider_id IN (…);   -- 0
DESCRIBE HISTORY silver.trips;                             -- operation = DELETE, with metrics
SELECT count(*) FROM silver.trips VERSION AS OF <v-1>
  WHERE rider_id IN (…);                                   -- 29  <- still there!

That last line is the teaching moment: the rows are gone from the current version but still present in time travel. The erasure is not complete until VACUUM removes the unreferenced files, and VACUUM is therefore a governance decision, not a storage chore.

The second trap: GPS. gps_events has no rider_id, so WHERE rider_id IN (…) matches nothing there — yet the pings are precise location data for the same trips. A correct erasure joins through trip_id. A team that forgets this passes their own test and fails an audit.

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: Compliance is a data-engineering property. Without ACID deletes, an erasure means rewriting a whole partition and hoping no reader saw the intermediate state; with no lineage, you cannot even enumerate where the subject's data went.

docs.title: Fixture — incident_speed_unit/ — THE signature incident
docs.text: File: gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson.gz (47,583 events, canonical gps_events schema — byte-for-byte schema-compatible with the 2026-06-05 raw feed) Used by: Lab 5 (streaming ingest), Lab 6 (observability / drift), Lab 8 (AI serving), Module 8 ETA-model degradation narrative. This is the incident the whole course keeps coming back to.

docs.title: What is wrong
docs.text:
On 2026-06-05, a device-firmware rollout moved 34% of the fleet (1,004 vehicles) from producer_version 2.4.0 to 2.5.0, starting at 09:00 UTC (12:00 Riyadh).

The new firmware kept the field name speed_kmh and its type (double) — and started writing metres per second.

{"...":"...","payload":{"lat":24.71,"lon":46.68,"speed_kmh":11.2, ...},"producer_version":"2.5.0"}
                                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                                         40.3 km/h reported as 11.2 — same key, same type
value events in this batch 47,583 distinct vehicles affected 1,004 mean speed_kmh if the field were km/h 35.45 mean speed_kmh as shipped (m/s) 9.85 ratio 3.60× (i.e. 3.6, the m/s → km/h factor)

docs.title: Why nothing catches it
docs.text:
• Schema validation passes. Same keys, same JSON types, same nesting. A StructType check, an Avro/Protobuf compatibility check and a MERGE SCHEMA all say "compatible".
  • Range checks pass. 11.2 is a perfectly plausible speed. So is 0.5. So is 38. Any expect_column_values_to_be_between("speed_kmh", 0, 200) is satisfied — in fact the corrupted data is further inside the range than the good data.
  • Row counts, freshness and volume are all normal. The feed is healthy by every operational signal.
  • No error is ever raised. Not at ingest, not in the stream, not in dbt.

docs.title: What it actually breaks
docs.text: gold.eta_features.rolling_avg_speed_10m is computed from payload.speed_kmh. For the affected vehicles it silently falls by 3.6×. The ETA model then learns "this zone is crawling" for a third of the fleet and starts over-predicting journey times — the ride-hailing symptom is quoted ETAs drifting long, riders cancelling, and a demand model that under-serves the affected zones. The model metrics degrade slowly; nobody links it to a firmware note in a device changelog.

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
The only things that catch this, in order of how fast they would have:

  1. Distribution drift on speed_kmh, segmented by producer_version. mean(speed_kmh) WHERE producer_version='2.5.0' ≈ 9.8 vs ≈ 35.5 for 2.4.0 on the same zones and hours. PSI/KS between the two version cohorts blows past any threshold. Always segment drift by producer version.
  2. A cross-field physical-plausibility check: reconcile distance_km / duration_min from silver.trips against the mean ping speed for the same trip_id. The two disagree by 3.6× only for v2.5.0 trips. This is a reconciliation check — the top of the data-quality pyramid, and the only tier that compares two independent measurements of the same physical fact.
  3. A unit-carrying contract. If the field were speed_mps or the payload carried "speed_unit":"km/h", the producer change would have been a breaking schema change and the pipeline would have failed loudly on day one.
  4. Lineage + a producer_version dimension. Once drift fires, producer_version is the first column to group by; without it in bronze, the investigation has nothing to correlate against.

docs.title: How to run it
docs.text:
# baseline: ingest the clean day
python3 generators/emit_gps_stream.py --file data/raw/gps/gps_2026-06-05.ndjson.gz

# then the incident batch
python3 generators/emit_gps_stream.py --file data/fixtures/incident_speed_unit/gps_2026-06-05_v250.ndjson.gz
# or, equivalently, synthesise it live:
python3 generators/emit_gps_stream.py --file data/raw/gps/gps_2026-06-05.ndjson.gz --inject unit-shift

Then compute rolling_avg_speed_10m over the combined bronze and plot it by hour: the break is at 09:00 UTC and it is obvious once you know to look. That gap — between "obvious in hindsight" and "invisible in flight" — is the point of the whole module.

docs.title: The unifying question
docs.text:
"What happens to Masar's AI system if THIS part of the data platform fails?"

Here nothing failed. Every component did exactly what it was told. The platform was healthy, the schema was valid, the tests were green, and the model got worse anyway — because type-compatibility is not semantic compatibility.

docs.title: Fixture — late_pings/
docs.text: File: gps_late_2026-06-04.ndjson (520 events, canonical gps_events schema plus one extra informational key, see below) Used by: Lab 5 (Streaming and Event-Driven Architectures) — the watermark drill.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
GPS pings with event times on 2026-06-04 that arrive after the stream has already moved past them. This is the normal condition for a mobility fleet: devices lose signal in tunnels, underground parking and roaming gaps, then flush a backlog when they reconnect.

property value total events 520 late by < 3 minutes (inside a 3-min watermark) ~284 late by 11–47 minutes (outside a 3-min watermark) ~216 duplicated event_ids within the batch 20 ordering shuffled — the file is deliberately not sorted by ts

Each record carries an extra _note_delay_seconds key stating how late it is. That key is instructional metadata, not part of the contract — strip it before producing to Kafka (emit_gps_stream.py --inject late does this for you), or keep it to grade the exercise.

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
Replay 2026-06-04's normal pings, then this file, into masar.gps.raw and run the event-time windowed aggregation:

.withWatermark("event_ts", "3 minutes")
.groupBy(window("event_ts", "5 minutes"), "pickup_zone_id")
  • Events late by < 3 min land in their correct 5-minute window; the window's count increases after it looked final. This is the point: watermarks let late data still be correct.
  • Events late by > 3 min are dropped — numRowsDroppedByWatermark in the streaming progress log is non-zero. Widen to withWatermark("event_ts", "60 minutes") and they reappear, at the cost of held state.
  • With no watermark at all, nothing is dropped but state grows without bound — watch stateOperators[0].numRowsTotal climb and never fall.
  • Duplicate event_ids prove that the watermark is about lateness, not deduplication: you still need dropDuplicates(["event_id"]) (bounded by the same watermark) or a MERGE on event_id.

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: Choosing a watermark is a trade-off, not a default. Too short silently discards real trips' telemetry (the ETA model's speed features go stale for exactly the vehicles that had connectivity problems); too long inflates state and delays every downstream result.

docs.title: Fixture — late_trips/
docs.text: File: trips_late_2026-06-02.csv (126 rows, canonical trips schema) Used by: Lab 3 (ETL vs ELT / dbt incremental) — the lookback-window drill. Also referenced by: Module 1 "two-tier divergence" simulation, Module 3 case study.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
Trips whose pickup_ts falls on 2026-06-02 but whose records only reached bronze on 2026-06-04 — two days late. In the real system this happens when a payment settles after the nightly cutoff, or a driver's device syncs after a tunnel/roaming gap.

  • 120 rows carry trip_ids that have never been seen upstream (prefix TRP-20260602-9……). These are the genuinely missing trips.
  • 6 rows are byte-identical re-sends of trip_ids that are already in bronze for 2026-06-02. They exist to prove the MERGE is idempotent.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
Land it as if it arrived on 2026-06-04:

cp trips_late_2026-06-02.csv ../../raw/trips_2026-06-02.late.csv   # or a second bronze batch

docs.title: Expected detection signal
docs.text:
Pipeline Result WHERE trip_date = current_date() (the bug) the 120 late trips are never counted — a silent ~2% undercount for 2026-06-02 3-day lookback + MERGE ON trip_id (the fix) 120 inserted, 6 matched no-ops, count for 2026-06-02 corrects itself Lookback but INSERT INTO instead of MERGE 6 duplicate trip_ids — the dbt unique test fails 1-day lookback still misses everything: the file is 2 days late — the window must exceed the observed lateness

Verify with: SELECT count(*) FROM silver.trips WHERE date(pickup_ts) = '2026-06-02' before and after. The delta must be exactly 120.

docs.title: Failure mode it teaches
docs.text: A silent correctness bug. No error, no failed test, no alert — just a daily number that is quietly low, which then trains the demand model and pays driver incentives on an undercount.

docs.title: LAB 00 — Environment Setup for the Masar Lakehouse
docs.text:
Send this document to participants T-minus 2 days. Complete it before Day 1 Hour 1. If anything on the acceptance checklist is red at 09:00 on Day 1, you will lose Lab 1 time.

Field Value Lab ID LAB-00 Module Pre-course (supports M1–M8) Day / Hour T-minus 2 days, self-paced Duration 45–60 min (30 min if you already have Python + Docker) Difficulty Foundational LO mapping Enables LO1–LO8; no LO assessed here Prerequisites Laptop with admin rights, 16 GB RAM recommended (8 GB workable), 20 GB free disk, GitHub account Checkpoint git tag lab0-setup (branch main also works) Deliverable A green make doctor report pasted into the course chat, plus SETUP_NOTES.md recording your fallback plan

Scale note. The figures in this document describe the shipped sample (--scale 0.15): 7,230 trips/day over 5 days (36,150 trips), 873,763 GPS pings, 3,450 drivers, 3,864 vehicles, 48 zones. Every other lab quotes the full-scale generator run (--scale 1.0) — 48,200 trips/day — so the row counts there are larger by design. Regenerate at --scale 1.0 (see data/README.md) if you want them to match.

docs.title: Why this lab matters
docs.text: The course question is "What happens to Masar's AI system if this part of the data platform fails?" — and the first thing that fails is the platform nobody could start. Every lab from Day 1 Hour 3 onward writes into the same masar-lakehouse/ working tree: Lab 1 lands bronze, Lab 3 transforms it to silver, Lab 4 makes silver ACID, Labs 5–8 stream, test, orchestrate and serve it. A broken JAVA_HOME on Day 1 therefore costs you the capstone on Day 5, not just one hour. Setting the environment up now, with the pinned versions, is the cheapest risk reduction available to you: Spark 3.5 with delta-spark 3.2 on Java 17 is a narrow compatibility window, and every version drift you introduce becomes a debugging session that eats lab time. Treat this as the first engineering decision of the course: reproducible environments are part of a reproducible data platform.

docs.title: 0. What you are installing and why
docs.text:
Component Pinned version Used from Why this pin Python 3.11.x Day 1 PySpark 3.5 wheels and dbt-core 1.7 are validated on 3.11; 3.12 breaks several transitive deps Java (JDK) 17 (LTS) Day 1 Spark 3.5 runs on 11 or 17; the course pins 17. Java 21+ raises UnsupportedClassVersionError/module errors PySpark 3.5.x Lab 1 Delta 3.2 is compiled against Spark 3.5 only delta-spark 3.2.x Lab 1 Transaction log, MERGE, time travel (M4) dbt-core / dbt-spark 1.7.x Lab 3 incremental_strategy='merge' on file_format='delta' via the session method Great Expectations 0.18.x Lab 6 1.x renamed the API used by the shipped suites Kafka (bitnami, single broker) 3.7 image Lab 5 Event backbone for GPS pings Redis 7 Lab 8 Online feature store, keyspace masar:features:zone:{zone_id} Docker Desktop or Colima current Lab 5, Lab 8 Runs the Kafka + Redis stack

Rule of the course: do not "upgrade to latest". If a tool suggests an upgrade, decline. Pins are in requirements.txt.

docs.title: 1. Python 3.11
docs.text:
macOS (Homebrew) 

brew install python@3.11
python3.11 --version          # Python 3.11.x

Windows — download the 3.11 installer from python.org, tick Add python.exe to PATH, then in PowerShell: 

py -3.11 --version

Linux (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04) 

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3.11 python3.11-venv python3.11-dev
python3.11 --version

Verify you did not get 3.12/3.13: 

python3.11 -c "import sys; assert sys.version_info[:2]==(3,11), sys.version; print('python ok', sys.version.split()[0])"

docs.title: 2. Java 17
docs.text:
Spark is a JVM application; PySpark is a client to it. You need a JDK (not a JRE) and a correctly exported JAVA_HOME.

macOS 

brew install --cask temurin@17
/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17          # prints the JDK 17 path
echo 'export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"'                >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

Windows (PowerShell, admin) 

winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("JAVA_HOME","C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-17.0.11.9-hotspot","User")
# Close and reopen the terminal, then:
$env:JAVA_HOME

Linux 

sudo apt install -y openjdk-17-jdk
echo 'export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Verify: 

java -version        # openjdk version "17.0.x"
echo $JAVA_HOME      # must be non-empty and point at a JDK 17 directory

Expected: 

openjdk version "17.0.11" 2024-04-16
OpenJDK Runtime Environment Temurin-17.0.11+9 (build 17.0.11+9)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM Temurin-17.0.11+9 (build 17.0.11+9, mixed mode)

docs.title: 3. Clone the course repository and create the virtual environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/<sdaia-academy-org>/masar-lakehouse.git
cd masar-lakehouse
git checkout lab0-setup

python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate            # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip

Install the pinned stack (this is the single line from the T-2 email):

pip install "pyspark==3.5.*" "delta-spark==3.2.*" "dbt-core==1.7.*" "dbt-spark[session]==1.7.*" \
            "great-expectations==0.18.*" "kafka-python==2.0.*" "redis==5.0.*" \
            "pandas==2.2.*" "pyarrow==15.*" "python-dotenv==1.0.*"

Equivalent and preferred (identical pins, reproducible):

pip install -r requirements.txt

Repository layout you should now see (this is the layout every lab refers to — do not rearrange it):

masar-lakehouse/
  data/raw/            trips_YYYY-MM-DD.csv | gps/gps_YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson | drivers.csv | vehicles.csv
                       zones.csv | payments_YYYY-MM-DD.csv | weather_hourly.csv
  data/fixtures/       corrections/ late_trips/ dirty_batch/ currency_shift/ erasure_request/
  lakehouse/bronze|silver|gold/     Delta tables (object-storage-style layout)
  src/masar/           spark.py ingest/ delta/ stream/ quality/ transform/ serve/ governance/ econ/
  dbt/masar/           dbt_project.yml profiles.yml models/staging models/marts/silver
  quality/suites/      silver_trips_suite.py  gps_events_suite.py
  orchestration/dags/  masar_medallion.py
  scripts/             doctor.py  make_targets
  Makefile  docker-compose.yml  requirements.txt

Make the package importable (the labs run modules as python -m masar.…):

pip install -e .        # or: export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src

Smoke-test Spark + Delta in one command:

python - <<'PY'
from masar.spark import get_spark
spark = get_spark("setup-check")
spark.range(5).write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/tmp/masar_delta_check")
print("delta rows:", spark.read.format("delta").load("/tmp/masar_delta_check").count())
spark.stop()
PY

Expected (Spark's first run downloads the Delta jars — allow 1–2 minutes and a wall of INFO lines):

:: loading settings :: url = jar:file:/.../ivy-2.5.1.jar!/org/apache/ivy/core/settings/ivysettings.xml
io.delta#delta-spark_2.12 added as a dependency
:: resolution report :: resolve 1284ms :: artifacts dl 41ms
delta rows: 5

docs.title: 4. Docker Desktop or Colima
docs.text:
The Kafka + Redis stack runs in containers. Pick one runtime.

Docker Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux) — install from docker.com. On Windows this requires WSL2:

wsl --install -d Ubuntu-22.04
wsl --set-default-version 2
# In Docker Desktop: Settings > Resources > WSL Integration > enable your distro

Colima (macOS, lighter, no Docker Desktop licence question):

brew install colima docker docker-compose
colima start --cpu 4 --memory 8 --disk 40

Verify either runtime:

docker run --rm hello-world
docker compose version        # v2.x; note the space, not docker-compose

docs.title: 5. Bring up the Kafka + Redis stack
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml ships with the repo (single-broker KRaft Kafka + Redis 7):

docker compose up -d
docker compose ps

Expected:

NAME               IMAGE                     STATUS                   PORTS
masar-kafka        bitnami/kafka:3.7         Up 34 seconds (healthy)  0.0.0.0:9092->9092/tcp
masar-redis        redis:7-alpine            Up 34 seconds (healthy)  0.0.0.0:6379->6379/tcp

Prove a round trip (do this now — Lab 5 is the boot-time risk of the whole course):

# create the topic used by Lab 5
docker exec masar-kafka kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --create --if-not-exists --topic masar.gps.raw --partitions 3 --replication-factor 1

docker exec masar-kafka kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --list

# produce + consume one test message
echo '{"event_id":"setup-check"}' | docker exec -i masar-kafka \
  kafka-console-producer.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --topic masar.gps.raw

docker exec masar-kafka kafka-console-consumer.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --topic masar.gps.raw --from-beginning --max-messages 1 --timeout-ms 10000

# redis
docker exec masar-redis redis-cli ping

Expected:

Created topic masar.gps.raw.
masar.gps.raw
{"event_id":"setup-check"}
Processed a total of 1 messages
PONG

Pre-pull the images even if you will not run the stack until Day 4 — classroom networks are slower than yours:

docker compose pull

Stop the stack when you are done (data is not needed until Day 4):

docker compose down          # add -v only if you want to discard Kafka volumes

docs.title: 6. Generate / verify the Masar sample data
docs.text:
The synthetic Masar dataset is generated with a pinned seed so every participant's row counts match the labs.

make data                    # runs data/generators with the pinned seed
ls -lh data/raw | head
wc -l data/raw/trips_2026-06-01.csv
head -1 data/raw/trips_2026-06-01.csv
zcat data/raw/gps/gps_2026-06-01.ndjson.gz | head -c 300; echo   # shipped gzipped

Expected:

trips_2026-06-01.csv   1.1M
trips_2026-06-02.csv   1.1M
drivers.csv            406K

docs.title: 10. Self-check questions
docs.text:
Q1. Why does this course pin Java 17 rather than "whatever JDK is installed"?

Answer Spark 3.5 supports Java 8/11/17 only. A newer JDK (21+) produces `UnsupportedClassVersionError` or module-access errors (`InaccessibleObjectException`) because Spark's reflective access to `java.nio` is blocked by the module system. Pinning the JDK is the same discipline as pinning the table format version: the platform must be reproducible before it can be trusted.

Q2. You run the Delta smoke test and get Delta ... is not a valid Spark SQL Data Source. What is wrong, and what is not wrong?

Answer The `delta-spark` package is installed but the session was built without the Delta extensions (`spark.sql.extensions` and the `DeltaCatalog`). The data, the JDK and the pip install are all fine. Always build the session with `get_spark()`; never construct `SparkSession.builder` ad hoc in a notebook.

Q3. Why does the course ask you to bring up Kafka on T-2 when the streaming lab is on Day 4?

Answer Image pulls and port conflicts are the highest-frequency Day-4 failure, and they are slow to fix on a shared classroom network. Pulling images and proving one produce/consume round trip now converts a 40-minute classroom outage into a 3-minute setup step at home.

Q4. Your organisation's laptop cannot install Docker. Which labs are affected and what is the mitigation?

Answer Lab 5 (Kafka streaming) and Lab 8's online store (Redis). Mitigation: use the instructor's shared broker for Lab 5 (bootstrap address issued Day 4) and the instructor's shared Redis for Lab 8 (`MASAR_REDIS_HOST` in your `.env` — `src/masar/serve/materialize_online.py` reads it, no code change). If neither is reachable, run Lab 8's offline half (`gold.eta_features`, the leakage drill, the BI star) and pair with someone who has Docker for the materialisation and consistency check. Labs 1–4, 6 and 7 are unaffected because they are pure Spark + Delta on local storage.

Q5. Why is lakehouse/ a local directory in this course, and what does it stand in for?

Answer It is a stand-in for an object-storage bucket (`s3://masar-lakehouse/`). The point of Module 2 is compute–storage separation: the Spark JVM is the compute, `lakehouse/` is the storage. Keeping the layout `zone/table/partition/` identical to a bucket means the same code runs unchanged against S3/ADLS.
