docs.title: PA-1 — Delta Recovery: A Vacuumed Table and a Non-Idempotent Merge
docs.text:
Field Value Assessment ID PA-1 Module M4 — Delta Lake and ACID Transactions Day / Hour Day 3, end of Hour 5 (immediately after the Lab-4 wrap) Duration 30 minutes, individual, open-repository / closed-collaboration LO mapping LO4 (primary) · LO6 (audit and retention governance) · LO3 (idempotent upsert) Weight Half of the 20% practical-assessment band (PA-1 + PA-2 + PA-3 → 20%) Sandbox ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips — a copy of silver.trips with the identical schema and grain. The participant's own silver.trips is never touched. Marking Diagnosis 40% · Fixes 40% · Verification evidence 20%

The course question, applied: "What happens to Masar's AI system if THIS part of the data platform fails?" Here it fails twice at once: the platform can no longer prove what it contained yesterday, and every corrections run silently multiplies trips. The demand mart inflates, the ETA training set gains phantom rows, and the audit trail that would have shown you both is gone.

Scale note. Figures quoted in this document assume the full-scale generator run (--scale 1.0); the shipped sample is --scale 0.15 — 7,230 trips/day over 5 days (36,150 trips), 873,763 GPS pings, 3,450 drivers, 3,864 vehicles, 48 zones. Grains, ratios and file-count reductions hold at either scale; absolute row counts do not.

docs.title: 1. Instructor setup
docs.text:
Run this before the session. It takes ~90 seconds and produces the broken starting state for every participant. Distribute the resulting directory, or have each participant run make pa1-setup (the target wraps this script).

# scripts/assessments/pa1_setup.py
"""PA-1 setup: build a Delta table with (a) destroyed time travel and
(b) a non-idempotent corrections job.

Run:  python -m scripts.assessments.pa1_setup
Idempotent: the sandbox is deleted and rebuilt on every run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from delta.tables import DeltaTable
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

from masar.spark import get_spark

SOURCE  = "./lakehouse/silver/trips"                    # the cohort's real silver table
SANDBOX = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips"
CORRECT = "data/fixtures/corrections/trips_corrections_2026-06-03.csv"


def main() -> None:
    spark = get_spark("pa1-setup")
    shutil.rmtree(Path(SANDBOX).parent, ignore_errors=True)

    # ---- v0: a clean copy of silver.trips (schema and grain identical) -----
    src = spark.read.format("delta").load(SOURCE)
    src.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(SANDBOX)
    spark.sql(f"ALTER TABLE delta.`{SANDBOX}` "
              f"ADD CONSTRAINT positive_fare CHECK (fare_sar > 0)")

    tgt = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, SANDBOX)
    schema = spark.read.format("delta").load(SANDBOX).schema
    corr = spark.read.option("header", True).schema(schema).csv(CORRECT)

    # ---- v1: a legitimate, idempotent correction (so history is meaningful)
    (tgt.alias("t").merge(corr.alias("s"), "t.trip_id = s.trip_id")
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll().execute())

    # ---- v2, v3: the NON-IDEMPOTENT job, run twice ------------------------
    # The match condition includes a per-run column, so nothing ever matches
    # and every run falls through to whenNotMatchedInsertAll.
    for _ in range(2):
        stamped = corr.withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())
        (tgt.alias("t")
            .merge(stamped.alias("s"),
                   "t.trip_id = s.trip_id AND t._ingested_at = s._ingested_at")
            .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
            .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
            .execute())

    # ---- v4: time travel destroyed ----------------------------------------
    spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck.enabled", "false")
    spark.sql(f"VACUUM delta.`{SANDBOX}` RETAIN 0 HOURS")
    spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck.enabled", "true")

    n = spark.read.format("delta").load(SANDBOX).count()
    d = spark.read.format("delta").load(SANDBOX).select("trip_id").distinct().count()
    print(f"[pa1-setup] rows={n:,} distinct trip_id={d:,} (expect {n-d:,} duplicate rows)")
    print(f"[pa1-setup] sandbox ready at {SANDBOX}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The participant is also given the broken job, verbatim, as the file they must repair:

# src/masar/delta/apply_corrections_pa1.py   <-- SHIPPED BROKEN. This is the artefact under test.
"""Apply the daily corrections file to the PA-1 trips table."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from delta.tables import DeltaTable
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

from masar.spark import get_spark

TABLE = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips"


def apply_corrections(path: str) -> None:
    spark = get_spark("pa1-corrections")
    schema = spark.read.format("delta").load(TABLE).schema
    corr = (spark.read.option("header", True).schema(schema).csv(path)
                 .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp()))

    target = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, TABLE)
    (target.alias("t")
        .merge(corr.alias("s"),
               "t.trip_id = s.trip_id AND t._ingested_at = s._ingested_at")
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute())
    print("corrections applied")


def maintain() -> None:
    """Nightly maintenance."""
    spark = get_spark("pa1-maintenance")
    spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck.enabled", "false")
    spark.sql(f"OPTIMIZE delta.`{TABLE}` ZORDER BY (city, pickup_ts)")
    spark.sql(f"VACUUM delta.`{TABLE}` RETAIN 0 HOURS")
    print("maintenance done")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--corrections")
    p.add_argument("--maintain", action="store_true")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if a.corrections:
        apply_corrections(a.corrections)
    if a.maintain:
        maintain()

docs.title: 2. Participant brief (hand this page out)
docs.text:
PA-1 — Delta Recovery · 30 minutes · individual

Masar's overnight corrections job has been running for four days. This morning the demand mart shows more completed trips than the platform ingested, and when Compliance asked what silver.trips contained before Tuesday's corrections, the query failed.

You have been handed the table and the job that maintains it:

  • Table: ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips (a copy of silver.trips, same schema, same intended grain: one row per trip_id)
  • Job: src/masar/delta/apply_corrections_pa1.py
  • Corrections fixture: data/fixtures/corrections/trips_corrections_2026-06-03.csv (5 rows)

Your task, in order:

  1. Diagnose. Find every defect in the table state and in the job. For each, state the mechanism — not "the merge is broken" but why the merge condition never matches — and the consumer-visible consequence in Masar terms (which mart, which model, which number).
  2. Fix. Repair the job so that (a) applying the corrections twice leaves the table identical, and (b) maintenance is safe to schedule. Restore the table to its correct grain. You may not rebuild the table from silver.trips — the point is recovery, and in production the source would be gone.
  3. Prove it. Produce evidence a reviewer can check without re-running anything: before/after counts, both operationMetrics blocks, the DESCRIBE HISTORY timeline, and a statement of what time travel can and cannot now do.

Constraints - Do not disable spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck. - Do not delete _delta_log. - Keep the schema unchanged; the grain is one row per trip_id. - Everything you write must be committed on branch pa1/<your-name>.

Deliverable artefacts (all three required):

Artefact Content PA1_DIAGNOSIS.md One numbered entry per defect: symptom → mechanism → consumer consequence → evidence line src/masar/delta/apply_corrections_pa1.py The repaired job (both apply_corrections and maintain) PA1_EVIDENCE.md Command transcripts proving idempotency, the restored grain, and the retention decision, with a one-paragraph statement of what history was permanently lost and what that costs

Time budget suggestion: 8 min diagnose · 12 min fix · 7 min evidence · 3 min commit.

docs.title: 4a. PA1_DIAGNOSIS.md
docs.text:
Defect 1 — the corrections MERGE is not idempotent. Symptom: DESCRIBE HISTORY shows v2 and v3 both reporting numTargetRowsInserted -> 5, numTargetRowsUpdated -> 0, for a corrections file containing 5 trip_ids that already exist in the table. Mechanism: the match condition is t.trip_id = s.trip_id AND t._ingested_at = s._ingested_at, and _ingested_at is stamped with F.current_timestamp() on the source at read time. The target's _ingested_at is whatever the previous run wrote. The two can never be equal across runs, so whenMatched never fires and control falls through to whenNotMatchedInsertAll — the job appends a fresh copy of all 5 corrections every night. Consumer consequence: the table's grain (one row per trip_id) is broken, so gold.zone_hourly_demand over-counts the affected zone-hours, gold.driver_daily over-counts those drivers' trips and revenue, and gold.eta_features gains duplicated training rows for the same trip — which also corrupts a time-based train/test split. The BI star and the demand mart stop reconciling, which is the two-tier divergence symptom appearing inside a single platform. Evidence: rows=42,048 distinct_trip_id=42,038 — surplus 10 = 5 corrections × 2 runs.

Defect 2 — VACUUM ... RETAIN 0 HOURS with the safety check disabled. Symptom: SELECT COUNT(*) ... VERSION AS OF 1 raises FileNotFoundException naming a Parquet file listed in the log. Mechanism: maintain() sets spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck.enabled = false and vacuums with zero retention, so every data file not referenced by the current snapshot is deleted immediately. The transaction log still describes versions 0–3, but their files are gone: the log is intact and unusable. Consequence A (governance): the audit question "what did this table contain before Tuesday's corrections?" is now unanswerable from this table. The pre-correction fare values existed only in v0–v1. Consequence B (availability): zero retention also deletes files a concurrently running reader or streaming query is about to open, failing a healthy job with the same exception. This is why Delta requires an explicit override. Evidence: v4 VACUUM END {numDeletedFiles -> 16} followed by the failing VERSION AS OF 1.

Defect 3 — the table is currently out of contract. Symptom: 10 surplus rows; the 5 corrected trip_ids each appear three times (the original, plus one insert per non-idempotent run). Mechanism: a consequence of Defect 1, but it must be repaired separately — fixing the job stops the bleeding and does not clean the wound. Consequence: as Defect 1. Note that the surplus rows are not identical: they carry different _ingested_at values, so a naive DISTINCT will not collapse them. Evidence: 

trip_id                copies  ingested_at_values
trp_20260601_004417    3       2026-06-19 19:07 / 2026-06-22 02:00 / 2026-06-23 02:00

What I cannot determine from this table alone: whether any other corrections file was applied by the same job on earlier nights. The _batch_id and _source_file lineage columns on bronze.trips would answer it; that is where I would look next, and it is why bronze exists.

docs.title: 4b. The repaired job
docs.text:
# src/masar/delta/apply_corrections_pa1.py   (repaired)
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from delta.tables import DeltaTable
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

from masar.spark import get_spark

TABLE = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips"
RETENTION_HOURS = 168          # 7 days. Justified in PA1_EVIDENCE.md.


def apply_corrections(path: str) -> None:
    """MERGE keyed on the BUSINESS key only. Re-running is a no-op."""
    spark = get_spark("pa1-corrections")
    schema = spark.read.format("delta").load(TABLE).schema
    corr = (spark.read.option("header", True).schema(schema).csv(path)
                 .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp()))

    # F2: the source must be one row per key, or whenMatchedUpdateAll is ambiguous.
    dupes = corr.groupBy("trip_id").count().filter("count > 1").count()
    if dupes:
        raise ValueError(f"{dupes} duplicate trip_id in {path}: MERGE would be ambiguous")

    target = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, TABLE)
    (target.alias("t")
        .merge(corr.alias("s"), "t.trip_id = s.trip_id")   # F1: business key only
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute())

    m = (spark.sql(f"DESCRIBE HISTORY delta.`{TABLE}` LIMIT 1")
              .select("version", "operationMetrics").first())
    print(f"v{m['version']} MERGE updated={m['operationMetrics'].get('numTargetRowsUpdated')} "
          f"inserted={m['operationMetrics'].get('numTargetRowsInserted')}")


def restore_grain() -> None:
    """F3: repair the damage already done, in place. Keep the LATEST row per key.

    Rationale for 'latest': every surplus row is a re-insertion of the same
    correction, so all copies carry identical business values; the newest
    _ingested_at is the one whose lineage matches the most recent run. The
    rule is therefore lossless here, and it is stated before it is executed.
    """
    spark = get_spark("pa1-restore-grain")
    df = spark.read.format("delta").load(TABLE)
    surplus = df.count() - df.select("trip_id").distinct().count()
    print(f"[grain] surplus rows before: {surplus}")

    keep = (df.withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(
                __import__("pyspark.sql.window", fromlist=["Window"]).Window
                .partitionBy("trip_id").orderBy(F.col("_ingested_at").desc())))
              .filter("_rn = 1").drop("_rn"))

    # Atomic replacement: one commit, readers never see a partial table.
    keep.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").option("overwriteSchema", "false").save(TABLE)

    df2 = spark.read.format("delta").load(TABLE)
    print(f"[grain] rows={df2.count():,} distinct trip_id={df2.select('trip_id').distinct().count():,}")


def maintain() -> None:
    """F4: safe, schedulable maintenance. The retention check stays ON."""
    spark = get_spark("pa1-maintenance")
    before = spark.sql(f"DESCRIBE DETAIL delta.`{TABLE}`").first()["numFiles"]
    spark.sql(f"OPTIMIZE delta.`{TABLE}` ZORDER BY (city, pickup_ts)")
    after = spark.sql(f"DESCRIBE DETAIL delta.`{TABLE}`").first()["numFiles"]
    print(f"[maintain] numFiles {before} -> {after}")

    spark.sql(f"VACUUM delta.`{TABLE}` RETAIN {RETENTION_HOURS} HOURS DRY RUN").show(5, False)
    spark.sql(f"VACUUM delta.`{TABLE}` RETAIN {RETENTION_HOURS} HOURS").show(truncate=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--corrections")
    p.add_argument("--restore-grain", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--maintain", action="store_true")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if a.restore_grain:
        restore_grain()
    if a.corrections:
        apply_corrections(a.corrections)
    if a.maintain:
        maintain()

Marker's note on restore_grain. An overwrite here is correct and is not the "overwrite where a MERGE was needed" anti-pattern: the operation intentionally replaces the whole table with a de-duplicated projection of itself, in one atomic commit, and it is a one-off repair rather than a scheduled write. Accept an equivalent DeltaTable.delete on a computed surplus predicate, or a MERGE-based rewrite, provided the participant states why the rule is lossless. Reject any repair that reads from silver.trips.

$ python -m masar.tools.sql --query "
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delta.\`./lakehouse/_assessments/pa1/trips\` VERSION AS OF 1"
java.io.FileNotFoundException: ... part-00003-....snappy.parquet

What was permanently lost, and what it costs. Versions 0–3 remain described in _delta_log but their data files were deleted by the RETAIN 0 HOURS vacuum, so the table can no longer answer "what were these five fares before Tuesday's correction?" That is exactly the question a fare dispute or a regulator's audit asks, and this table can no longer answer it. The platform is not entirely blind: bronze.trips is append-only and still holds the raw rows with _source_file and _batch_id, so the pre-correction values are re-derivable by replaying the silver transform against a bronze snapshot — slower, and it proves what the source said rather than what the table served, which is a weaker form of evidence. Time travel from v5 onward is intact and is the version floor for any future audit.

Retention decision: RETAIN 168 HOURS. Three inputs. (a) Audit window: Masar's fare-dispute process runs to five working days, so the live table must serve seven days of prior versions. (b) PDPL: an honoured erasure must not leave personal data physically recoverable indefinitely; seven days bounds the gap between the DELETE commit and physical removal, and the erasure runbook schedules a VACUUM after that window rather than relying on the nightly job. (c) Storage: seven days of tombstoned files on this table is under 5 MB at lab scale and a few GB at production scale — cheap relative to both other constraints. What would change the number: a longer statutory dispute window pushes it up; a stricter erasure SLA pushes it down; neither justifies zero, because zero also breaks concurrent readers.

docs.title: 5. Instructor delivery notes
docs.text:
Timing. Announce 30 minutes and hold it. At T+10 announce "you should be writing fixes now"; at T+22 announce "stop fixing, start evidencing" — participants who lose marks here almost always lose them on evidence, not on the repair.

What separates the bands in practice.

Observation Frequency What it signals Fixes the MERGE, forgets the 10 dirty rows Very high Understands the mechanism, has not yet internalised that fixing a pipeline does not fix its output. Ask: "your job is now correct — is your table?" Rebuilds the sandbox from silver.trips High The prohibited shortcut. In production the source is gone; the whole point is in-place recovery Diagnoses RETAIN 0 only as "loses time travel" High Half marks on D2. The concurrency consequence is what makes it an availability bug, not just a governance one Re-disables retentionDurationCheck to "test" the fix Medium Automatic cap. Have them re-read the guardrail's error text Claims idempotency after a single run Medium E1 unearned. Idempotency is a claim about the second run Notices that the surplus rows differ in _ingested_at and therefore that DISTINCT will not help Low Distinction signal — flag it in moderation

Live verification (30 seconds, during marking). Run the participant's apply_corrections twice on the marker's machine and check updated -> 0 on the second run. This is the single highest-value check and it settles the Fixes band on its own.

Capstone linkage. PA-1 assesses capstone requirement 4 (Delta Lake, LO4) in isolation, and the anti-pattern flags it tests — VACUUM RETAIN 0 and non-idempotent writes — are two of the six that cap a capstone criterion at 70%. A participant who fails PA-1 should be told explicitly which capstone criterion is at risk.

docs.title: PA-2 — Streaming: Exactly-Once Ingestion and an Event-Time Window
docs.text:
Field Value Assessment ID PA-2 Module M5 — Streaming Data and Event-Driven Architectures Day / Hour Day 4, end of Hour 5 (after the governance micro-lecture) Duration 30 minutes, individual, open-repository / closed-collaboration LO mapping LO5 (primary) · LO4 (Delta atomic commit as the idempotent sink) · LO6 (late-data correctness) Weight One third of the 20% practical-assessment band Sandbox Kafka topic masar.gps.pings.pa2 (3 partitions) → ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events and ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/zone_demand. The cohort's bronze.gps_events is never touched. Marking Correctness of fix 50% · Evidence 30% · Reasoning about semantics 20%

The course question, applied: "What happens to Masar's AI system if THIS part of the data platform fails?" A stream without a checkpoint invents vehicles. A processing-time window files a 20-minute-late ping under the wrong quarter-hour. Both errors flow into rolling_zone_demand_15m, so the ETA model predicts a rush hour that is not happening and surge pricing fires in an empty district — at Masar's scale, in a real city, for real riders.

docs.title: The broken job (the artefact under test)
docs.text:
# src/masar/stream/ingest_gps_pa2.py   <-- SHIPPED BROKEN
"""PA-2: land the PA-2 GPS topic into a Delta table and publish 15-minute
zone demand. Two queries, one file.

Written in a hurry by an engineer who was told the pipeline 'basically works'.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pyspark.sql import functions as F, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.types import (StructType, StructField, StringType,
                               DoubleType, TimestampType)

from masar.spark import get_spark

TOPIC     = "masar.gps.pings.pa2"
BOOTSTRAP = "localhost:9092"
BRONZE    = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events"
DEMAND    = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/zone_demand"

PAYLOAD_SCHEMA = StructType([
    StructField("lat",         DoubleType()),
    StructField("lon",         DoubleType()),
    StructField("speed_kmh",   DoubleType()),
    StructField("heading_deg", DoubleType()),
    StructField("accuracy_m",  DoubleType()),
])
PING_SCHEMA = StructType([
    StructField("event_id",         StringType()),
    StructField("vehicle_id",       StringType()),
    StructField("driver_id",        StringType()),
    StructField("trip_id",          StringType()),
    StructField("ts",               TimestampType()),
    StructField("payload",          PAYLOAD_SCHEMA),
    StructField("producer_version", StringType()),
])


def parse(raw: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    return (raw.select(
        F.from_json(F.col("value").cast("string"), PING_SCHEMA).alias("p"),
        F.col("topic"), F.col("partition"), F.col("offset"),
        F.col("timestamp").alias("_kafka_ts"))
        .select(
            F.col("p.event_id").alias("event_id"),
            F.col("p.vehicle_id").alias("vehicle_id"),
            F.col("p.driver_id").alias("driver_id"),
            F.col("p.trip_id").alias("trip_id"),
            F.col("p.ts").alias("ts"),
            F.col("p.payload").alias("payload"),
            F.col("p.producer_version").alias("producer_version"),
            F.col("_kafka_ts"),
            F.concat_ws("/", F.lit("kafka:/"), F.col("topic"),
                        F.col("partition").cast("string")).alias("_source_file"),
            F.col("offset").alias("_kafka_offset")))


def write_batch(batch_df: DataFrame, batch_id: int) -> None:
    out = (batch_df
           .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(batch_id).cast("long"))
           .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp()))
    (out.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(BRONZE))
    print(f"Batch {batch_id}: appended {out.count():,} pings", flush=True)


def run() -> None:
    spark = get_spark("pa2-gps")
    raw = (spark.readStream.format("kafka")
           .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", BOOTSTRAP)
           .option("subscribe", TOPIC)
           .option("startingOffsets", "earliest")
           .option("maxOffsetsPerTrigger", 8000)
           .load())
    events = parse(raw)

    # ---- query 1: land to bronze -----------------------------------------
    q1 = (events.writeStream
          .queryName("pa2_bronze")
          .foreachBatch(write_batch)
          .outputMode("append")
          .trigger(processingTime="20 seconds")
          .start())

    # ---- query 2: 15-minute zone demand ----------------------------------
    demand = (events
              .groupBy(F.window(F.current_timestamp(), "15 minutes"),
                       F.col("trip_id"))
              .agg(F.count("*").alias("pings")))

    q2 = (demand.writeStream
          .queryName("pa2_demand")
          .outputMode("complete")
          .format("delta")
          .option("checkpointLocation", "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/_ckpt")
          .trigger(processingTime="20 seconds")
          .start(DEMAND))

    q1.awaitTermination()
    q2.awaitTermination()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

docs.text:
$ python -m masar.stream.ingest_gps_pa2          # let it drain, then Ctrl-C and restart
Batch 0: appended 8,000 pings
Batch 1: appended 8,000 pings
^C
$ python -m masar.stream.ingest_gps_pa2
Batch 0: appended 8,000 pings                    <- batch 0 again: offsets were never committed
...
$ python -m masar.tools.count --table _assessments/pa2/gps_events
rows=56,000   distinct_event_id=39,842           <- 40,000 pings produced

Four faults are present. Tell participants there is more than one; do not say how many.

# Fault Where 1 Query 1 has no checkpointLocation — restart replays from earliest q1 2 Query 2 uses F.current_timestamp() — a processing-time window demand 3 No watermark on the aggregation, and outputMode("complete") — unbounded state demand 4 No idempotent-write guard on the sink (txnAppId / txnVersion), and the grain of query 2 is trip_id, not pickup_zone_id — it is not zone demand at all write_batch, demand

Fault 4 has two halves and is where the distinction band separates: the second half is a semantic error that no amount of streaming discipline would catch.

docs.title: 2. Participant brief (hand this page out)
docs.text:
PA-2 — Streaming Exactly-Once · 30 minutes · individual

The PA-2 GPS pipeline was written under time pressure and has been running for a week. Operations report two things: the zone-demand panel shows demand spikes that field staff cannot corroborate, and the row count in the landing table grows every time the job is restarted after a deploy.

You have:

  • Topic masar.gps.pings.pa2, 3 partitions, 40,000 pings already produced and keyed by trip_id. ~500 of them are back-dated 2–30 minutes (the late-ping fixture).
  • Job src/masar/stream/ingest_gps_pa2.py — two streaming queries in one file.
  • Sinks ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events and ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/zone_demand.

Your task, in order:

  1. Produce exactly-once ingestion. After your fix, a kill and restart mid-batch must leave the landing table with exactly one row per ping the producer sent. Source-level duplicate event_ids from the feed itself are a data problem — do not confuse them with pipeline duplicates, and say which is which in your evidence.
  2. Produce an event-time windowed zone demand with a watermark. The grain must be (pickup_zone_id, window); the window must be 15 minutes on the event's own timestamp; late data must be admitted within a stated lateness bound and dropped beyond it.
  3. Prove it. A kill/restart transcript with counts taken before the kill, immediately after the kill, and after the restart drains. State what your watermark costs you at both ends.

Constraints - Do not delete the sink table or its _delta_log to "reset". - Do not re-produce to the topic; the 40,000 pings are the fixed input. - Each query gets its own checkpoint directory. Do not share one. - Wire schema is fixed (CONVENTIONS): do not invent columns.

Deliverable artefacts (all three required):

Artefact Content src/masar/stream/ingest_gps_pa2.py The repaired job PA2_EVIDENCE.md The kill/restart proof table, the late-data table, and the consumer-lag reading, as pasted transcripts PA2_REASONING.md Where exactly-once is guaranteed and by which two mechanisms (name file paths, not concepts); why event time rather than processing time; your watermark value and what it costs at each end

Time budget suggestion: 10 min fix · 12 min run and prove · 5 min reasoning · 3 min commit.

docs.title: 3. Marking scheme
docs.text: Total 100. Pass ≥ 70 for badge contribution.

docs.title: 3a. Correctness of fix — 50 marks
docs.text:
Sub-criterion Marks What earns it C1. Dedicated checkpointLocation on every query, no sharing 12 Two distinct directories under ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/_checkpoints/<query_name> C2. Idempotent sink guard 8 txnAppId + txnVersion=batch_id on the bronze write (or an equivalent argued mechanism), so a replayed batch is a no-op C3. Event-time window 12 F.window(F.col("ts"), "15 minutes") — the event's own timestamp, not current_timestamp() and not _kafka_ts C4. Watermark present and bounded 10 withWatermark("ts", "<n> minutes") before the aggregation, with outputMode("append") or update rather than complete C5. Correct grain 8 Demand is aggregated at pickup_zone_id (joined from silver.trips on trip_id, or the zone carried on the ping), not at trip_id

Band descriptors — Correctness

Band Marks Descriptor Distinction 45–50 All five. The complete → append change is made deliberately and explained as a consequence of introducing a watermark. The grain error is found without prompting Proficient 35–44 Checkpoint, event time and watermark all correct; the idempotent-write guard or the grain is missed Developing 22–34 Checkpoint added (duplicates stop) but the aggregation is still processing-time, or event time adopted with no watermark so state grows unbounded Insufficient 0–21 Duplicates persist on restart, or the sink was deleted to make the counts look right

docs.title: 3b. Evidence — 30 marks
docs.text:
Sub-criterion Marks What earns it E1. Kill/restart proof table with three counts 12 Before kill / immediately after kill / after restart drains, each with rows and distinct event_id E2. Pipeline duplicates separated from source duplicates 8 States that rows − distinct event_id ≈ 0.4% is the seeded source defect and that pipeline-introduced duplicates = 0 is the number under test E3. Late-data evidence 6 Shows late pings landing in their event-time window, and reports the count dropped beyond the watermark (not zero, and explained) E4. Operational reading 4 Consumer-group lag captured and described as steady rather than growing

Band descriptors — Evidence

Band Marks Descriptor Distinction 27–30 All four, as transcripts. The participant kills the job mid-batch (not between batches) and says so, and reports the count taken immediately after the kill to show the interrupted batch did not partially commit Proficient 21–26 Kill/restart proven with three counts; the source-vs-pipeline duplicate distinction is stated but not evidenced, or the late-data drop count is missing Developing 12–20 A final count only, with no before/after; or the kill happened between batches, which proves nothing about atomicity Insufficient 0–11 No transcripts, or numbers that do not reconcile with 40,000 produced pings

docs.title: 3c. Reasoning about semantics — 20 marks
docs.text:
Sub-criterion Marks What earns it R1. Exactly-once located precisely 8 Names the composition — Kafka's replayable at-least-once source plus Delta's atomic, idempotent commit — and cites the actual checkpoint path and the txnAppId; says explicitly that neither component provides it alone R2. Event vs processing time justified with the data 6 Uses the observed lag (the fixture reaches ~1,798 s) to show that a processing-time window misfiles late pings into the current window R3. Watermark trade-off quantified at both ends 6 Too short → correct-but-late pings dropped and demand under-reports; too long → state and latency grow and windows finalise late. States the chosen value and what would change it

Band descriptors — Reasoning

Band Marks Descriptor Distinction 18–20 All three, with the consequence expressed in Masar terms (which feature, which model, which rider-visible behaviour). Volunteers what a shared checkpoint would have done Proficient 14–17 Correct mechanisms named; the watermark trade-off is stated in one direction only Developing 8–13 "Kafka gives exactly-once" or "the checkpoint fixes it" with no composition Insufficient 0–7 Absent or incorrect

docs.title: Automatic caps
docs.text: Condition Cap Sink table or _delta_log deleted to reset Overall capped at 50% Two queries sharing one checkpointLocation Correctness capped at 50% Aggregation still on processing time Correctness capped at 40% Kill/restart not demonstrated Evidence scores 0

docs.title: 4a. The repaired job (changed regions only)
docs.text:
BRONZE_CKPT = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/_checkpoints/pa2_bronze"    # C1: one per query
DEMAND_CKPT = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/_checkpoints/pa2_demand"    # C1
TXN_APP_ID  = "masar_pa2_gps_bronze"                                     # C2
WATERMARK   = "10 minutes"                                               # C4: see reasoning
ZONES       = "./lakehouse/silver/trips"                                 # C5: trip -> zone


def write_batch(batch_df: DataFrame, batch_id: int) -> None:
    out = (batch_df
           .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(batch_id).cast("long"))
           .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())
           .withColumn("ingest_date", F.to_date(F.col("_kafka_ts"))))
    (out.write.format("delta").mode("append")
        .partitionBy("ingest_date")
        .option("txnAppId", TXN_APP_ID)        # C2: replay of this batch_id is dropped
        .option("txnVersion", batch_id)
        .option("mergeSchema", "false")
        .save(BRONZE))
    print(f"Batch {batch_id}: appended {out.count():,} pings", flush=True)


def run() -> None:
    spark = get_spark("pa2-gps")
    raw = (spark.readStream.format("kafka")
           .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", BOOTSTRAP)
           .option("subscribe", TOPIC)
           .option("startingOffsets", "earliest")
           .option("maxOffsetsPerTrigger", 8000)
           .option("failOnDataLoss", "true")
           .load())
    events = parse(raw)

    # ---- query 1: land to bronze, exactly-once ---------------------------
    q1 = (events.writeStream
          .queryName("pa2_bronze")
          .foreachBatch(write_batch)
          .outputMode("append")
          .option("checkpointLocation", BRONZE_CKPT)     # C1
          .trigger(processingTime="20 seconds")
          .start())

    # ---- query 2: EVENT-TIME zone demand, watermarked --------------------
    # C5: the ping carries trip_id, not a zone. The zone is a property of the
    # trip, so resolve it from silver.trips - a static, broadcastable dimension.
    trip_zone = (spark.read.format("delta").load(ZONES)
                 .select("trip_id", "pickup_zone_id"))

    demand = (events
              .withWatermark("ts", WATERMARK)                       # C4
              .join(F.broadcast(trip_zone), "trip_id", "left")
              .groupBy(F.window(F.col("ts"), "15 minutes"),         # C3: event time
                       F.col("pickup_zone_id"))
              .agg(F.countDistinct("trip_id").alias("active_trips"),
                   F.count("*").alias("pings")))

    q2 = (demand.writeStream
          .queryName("pa2_demand")
          .outputMode("append")                # C4: append is the watermarked mode
          .format("delta")
          .option("checkpointLocation", DEMAND_CKPT)     # C1
          .trigger(processingTime="20 seconds")
          .start(DEMAND))

    spark.streams.awaitAnyTermination()

Marker's note. outputMode("update") with a Delta sink is not supported; a participant who keeps complete after adding a watermark has not understood that the watermark exists to let windows close. Accept append only. Accept countDistinct("trip_id") or a trip_id-level pre-aggregation for active_trips; reject a demand table whose grain is trip_id.

docs.title: 4b. PA2_EVIDENCE.md — the kill/restart proof transcript
docs.text:
# --- 1. Pre-kill state -------------------------------------------------------
$ python -m masar.stream.ingest_gps_pa2
Batch 0: appended 8,000 pings
Batch 1: appended 8,000 pings
Batch 2: appended 8,000 pings
^C                                   <- interrupted ~4s into batch 3, mid-flight

$ python -m masar.tools.sql --query "
    SELECT COUNT(*) rows, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) distinct_events
    FROM delta.\`./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events\`"
rows     distinct_events
24,000   23,904                      <- batch 3 did NOT partially commit

# --- 2. Restart. Change nothing. The checkpoint does the work. ---------------
$ python -m masar.stream.ingest_gps_pa2
Batch 3: appended 8,000 pings        <- resumes at batch 3, not batch 0
Batch 4: appended 8,000 pings
Batch 5: appended 0 pings

$ python -m masar.tools.sql --query "
    SELECT COUNT(*) rows, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) distinct_events
    FROM delta.\`./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events\`"
rows     distinct_events
40,000   39,842

Kill/restart proof table

Stage Pings produced Rows in sink Distinct event_id Source dupes Pipeline-introduced dupes After 3 clean batches 24,000 24,000 23,904 96 (0.40%) 0 Immediately after the mid-batch kill 24,000 24,000 23,904 96 0 After restart, drained 40,000 40,000 39,842 158 (0.40%) 0 (baseline: the broken job) 40,000 56,000 39,842 158 16,000

The last column is the number under test and it must be 0. rows − distinct event_id sits at 0.40% throughout — that is the seeded source defect described in CONVENTIONS (~0.4% duplicate event_id in the GPS feed), a data problem fixed by dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark at silver. Pipeline-introduced duplicates are an engineering problem, and the checkpoint is why there are none. Confusing the two is the most common way to fail this assessment while producing a correct pipeline.

Late-data evidence

$ python -m masar.tools.sql --query "
    SELECT window.start, pickup_zone_id, active_trips, pings
    FROM delta.\`./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/zone_demand\`
    WHERE pickup_zone_id = 'ZN-RUH-014' ORDER BY window.start"
window.start          pickup_zone_id  active_trips  pings
2026-06-30 07:45:00   ZN-RUH-014      31            744
2026-06-30 08:00:00   ZN-RUH-014      44            1,061
2026-06-30 08:15:00   ZN-RUH-014      39            938

$ python -m masar.tools.sql --query "
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS beyond_watermark
    FROM delta.\`./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/gps_events\` e
    WHERE UNIX_TIMESTAMP(e._kafka_ts) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(e.ts) > 600"
beyond_watermark
41

41 of the ~500 late pings arrived more than 10 minutes after their event time and were therefore excluded from their window. This number must not be zero: a watermark that drops nothing is either too generous or the fixture was not loaded. Under the broken processing-time window, all ~500 late pings were counted in whichever 15-minute window happened to be current when they were processed — inflating that window and leaving 07:45 under-reported.

Consumer lag

$ docker compose exec kafka kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
    --describe --all-groups | head
GROUP                          TOPIC                  PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
spark-kafka-source-pa2-bronze  masar.gps.pings.pa2    0          13361           13361           0
spark-kafka-source-pa2-bronze  masar.gps.pings.pa2    1          13298           13298           0
spark-kafka-source-pa2-bronze  masar.gps.pings.pa2    2          13341           13341           0

Lag is 0 and stable across all three partitions after drain. Under load the number that matters is not its absolute value but its derivative: a lag that grows monotonically means the trigger interval or maxOffsetsPerTrigger is mis-sized for the arrival rate, and the pipeline will never catch up on its own.

docs.title: 4c. PA2_REASONING.md
docs.text:
Where exactly-once lives. Neither Kafka nor Delta provides it alone. Kafka provides durable, replayable at-least-once delivery — offsets survive and can be rewound. Delta provides an atomic, idempotent sink — a micro-batch commit is all-or-nothing, and txnAppId="masar_pa2_gps_bronze" with txnVersion=batch_id makes a replayed batch a no-op at the sink. Exactly-once is the composition, and it is materialised in exactly one place: ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa2/_checkpoints/pa2_bronze, which records which Kafka offsets were included in each committed Delta transaction. After the kill, the restart read that offset log, resumed at batch 3, and could not re-append what had already committed. The second query has its own checkpoint at _checkpoints/pa2_demand; had I pointed both at one directory, the second query would have read the first's offset log and state and either skipped data it never processed or replayed state that does not belong to it — and Spark does not reliably fail loudly when that happens, which is why one checkpoint per query is a rule and not a preference.

Why event time. The observed lag in this feed reaches 1,798 seconds — nearly 30 minutes. A window built on current_timestamp() files each ping under the quarter-hour in which the pipeline happened to see it, so a batch of pings from 07:50 that arrived at 08:19 inflates the 08:15 window and leaves 07:45 under-reported. Both errors are then read by rolling_zone_demand_15m, so the ETA model sees a rush hour that did not occur in a zone where it did not occur, and surge fires against phantom demand. Event time makes the answer a property of what happened; processing time makes it a property of how the pipeline was feeling. I keep _kafka_ts alongside ts because processing time is still the right clock for operational metrics — lag, staleness, alerting.

Watermark: 10 minutes. The fixture's late pings are back-dated 2–30 minutes, so 10 minutes admits the bulk of genuine mobile-network lateness and drops the long tail (41 pings, 8% of the late fixture). Too short — 30 seconds — drops correct-but-late pings, so demand systematically under-reports in exactly the congested zones where telemetry is slowest, which is a bias, not noise. Too long — 30 minutes — keeps window state for half an hour, growing memory and delaying every window's finalisation, so the demand feature the model reads is 30 minutes behind reality. Ten minutes is the point where the marginal ping recovered is worth less than the latency it costs. What would change it: a measured shift in the p99 of _kafka_ts − ts (this feed's is ~9 minutes), or a downstream consumer whose SLA cannot tolerate a 10-minute finalisation delay — in which case the correct move is a shorter watermark plus a scheduled late-data reconciliation batch, not a silently lossy stream.

docs.title: 5. Instructor delivery notes
docs.text:
Pre-flight. Kafka is the boot-time risk in this course. Bring the stack up and produce the fixture before the room arrives; a participant who spends 12 of their 30 minutes on a port clash is being assessed on Docker, not on streaming.

Timing. At T+12 announce "your fix should be running by now". At T+22, "stop tuning, capture your transcripts" — evidence is 30% and is the most commonly abandoned section.

What separates the bands in practice.

Observation Frequency What it signals Adds a checkpoint, leaves the processing-time window Very high Fixed the visible bug, missed the silent one. The duplicates were counted; the misfiled windows were not Kills between batches rather than mid-batch High E1 partially unearned — the proof is about atomicity of an interrupted batch Reports rows − distinct event_id = 158 as a pipeline failure High The source/pipeline duplicate confusion. Write both columns on the board and label them Deletes the sink to "start clean" before the proof Medium Automatic cap. In production the sink is the asset Keeps outputMode("complete") after adding a watermark Medium Has added the watermark as an incantation, not as the mechanism that lets a window close Notices the demand grain is trip_id, not pickup_zone_id Low Distinction signal — this is a semantic defect that perfect streaming discipline would still have shipped

Live verification (60 seconds, during marking). Ask the participant to kill their running job in front of you and restart it, then read the count aloud. This is the module's thesis and the assessment authorises checking it live.

Capstone linkage. PA-2 assesses capstone requirement 5 (Streaming, LO5) in isolation. Two of its faults are capstone anti-pattern flags that cap a criterion at 70%: streaming without a dedicated checkpoint and processing-time aggregation. A participant scoring below 70 here should be told which capstone criterion is at risk and pointed at Lab 5 Task 3 before Day 5.

docs.title: PA-3 — Feature Leakage Audit: gold.eta_features and a Model Card That Lies
docs.text:
Field Value Assessment ID PA-3 Module M8 — Serving Data to AI and BI Workloads Day / Hour Day 5, Hour 4 (first 30 minutes of capstone assembly, run as a timed individual break-out) Duration 30 minutes, individual, open-repository / closed-collaboration LO mapping LO8 (primary) · LO6 (governance at the serving boundary) · LO7 (point-in-time correctness of a gold product) · LO3 (the training join is an ELT join) Weight One third of the 20% practical-assessment band Sandbox ./lakehouse/_assessments/pa3/eta_features — a rebuild of gold.eta_features with the same 13 CONVENTIONS columns and a different defect mix from the Lab-8 starter. The participant's own gold.eta_features is never touched. Marking Classification 40% · Fixes and the point-in-time join 35% · Honest metric and reporting 25%

The course question, applied: "What happens to Masar's AI system if THIS part of the data platform fails?" Nothing visible. That is the point. Every check is green, every test passes, the model card reads R² 0.94, and the platform ships a model that will miss by three times what it promised — because the failure is not in the pipeline's mechanics but in when four of its numbers were written.

Scale note. Figures quoted in this document assume the full-scale generator run (--scale 1.0); the shipped sample is --scale 0.15 — 7,230 trips/day over 5 days (36,150 trips), 873,763 GPS pings, 3,450 drivers, 3,864 vehicles, 48 zones. Grains, ratios and file-count reductions hold at either scale; absolute row counts do not.

docs.title: 1. Why this exists separately from the Lab-8 drill
docs.text:
Lab 8 Task 3 runs the leakage drill in pairs, with the instructor in the room and the diagnostics supplied. PA-3 is the individually assessed transfer test: the same 13-column contract, a different defect mix, no supplied diagnostics, no pair.

Two columns deliberately swap class relative to the lab. A participant who memorised the Lab-8 answer key will get both wrong:

Column Lab-8 starter PA-3 variant rolling_avg_speed_10m LEAKAGE (averaged the trip's own pings) VALID — correctly computed from other vehicles' pings strictly before feature_ts historical_route_duration VALID (rangeBetween(-2592000, -1)) LEAKAGE — the bound is now (-2592000, 0), so the current trip's own duration is inside its own 30-day average

The class tally is identical to the lab's (7 VALID / 1 STALE / 4 LEAKAGE / 1 UNAVAILABLE ONLINE), which is deliberate: a participant who counts rather than reasons will still be wrong on two rows, and the tally gives them no signal.

If PA-3 is delivered before Lab 8 (a cohort running the assessment early, or a re-sit before the drill), use the same variant — nothing in it depends on having seen the lab. Note in the moderation record which order the cohort experienced, because the difficulty is not identical.

docs.title: 2. Instructor setup
docs.text:
# scripts/assessments/pa3_setup.py
"""PA-3 setup: build the PA-3 variant of gold.eta_features.

EXACTLY the 13 CONVENTIONS columns. Five defects, listed in the answer key.
Run:  python -m scripts.assessments.pa3_setup
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from pyspark.sql import functions as F, Window

from masar.spark import get_spark

SILVER_TRIPS     = "./lakehouse/silver/trips"
SILVER_POSITIONS = "./lakehouse/silver/vehicle_positions"
WEATHER          = "data/raw/weather_hourly.csv"
OUT              = "./lakehouse/_assessments/pa3/eta_features"


def main() -> None:
    spark = get_spark("pa3-setup")
    shutil.rmtree(Path(OUT).parent, ignore_errors=True)

    trips = (spark.read.format("delta").load(SILVER_TRIPS)
             .filter(F.col("status") == "completed")
             .withColumn("pickup_epoch", F.col("pickup_ts").cast("long")))
    pos = spark.read.format("delta").load(SILVER_POSITIONS)
    weather = (spark.read.option("header", True).option("inferSchema", True).csv(WEATHER)
               .withColumn("hour_ts", F.to_timestamp("hour_ts")))

    # (A) DEFECT 1 - zone demand: inclusive upper bound admits same-second trips.
    w_demand = (Window.partitionBy("city", "pickup_zone_id")
                      .orderBy("pickup_epoch").rangeBetween(-900, 0))

    # (B) driver recent trips: bound is correct; the STALENESS is an online problem.
    w_driver = (Window.partitionBy("driver_id")
                      .orderBy("pickup_epoch").rangeBetween(-86400, -1))

    # (C) DEFECT 2 - historical route duration: upper bound 0 puts the trip's own
    #     duration inside its own 30-day route average.
    w_route = (Window.partitionBy("pickup_zone_id", "dropoff_zone_id")
                     .orderBy("pickup_epoch").rangeBetween(-2592000, 0))

    # (D) rolling average speed - CORRECT in this variant: other vehicles in the
    #     pickup zone, strictly before feature_ts, this trip excluded.
    zone_speed = (pos.alias("p")
        .join(trips.alias("t2").select(F.col("trip_id").alias("t2_trip"),
                                       F.col("pickup_zone_id").alias("t2_zone")),
              F.col("p.trip_id") == F.col("t2_trip"), "inner")
        .select(F.col("p.trip_id").alias("src_trip"), "t2_zone",
                F.col("p.event_ts").alias("ping_ts"), F.col("p.speed_kmh")))

    feats = (trips
        .withColumn("rolling_zone_demand_15m", F.count("*").over(w_demand))
        .withColumn("driver_recent_trip_count", F.count("*").over(w_driver))
        .withColumn("historical_route_duration", F.avg("duration_min").over(w_route))
        .withColumn("hour_of_day", F.hour("pickup_ts"))
        .withColumn("day_of_week", F.dayofweek("pickup_ts"))
        .withColumn("feature_ts", F.col("pickup_ts")))

    speed_10m = (feats.alias("f").join(zone_speed.alias("z"),
            (F.col("f.pickup_zone_id") == F.col("z.t2_zone")) &
            (F.col("z.src_trip") != F.col("f.trip_id")) &
            (F.col("z.ping_ts") <  F.col("f.feature_ts")) &
            (F.col("z.ping_ts") >= F.expr("f.feature_ts - INTERVAL 10 MINUTES")), "left")
        .groupBy("f.trip_id").agg(F.avg("z.speed_kmh").alias("rolling_avg_speed_10m")))

    out = (feats.join(speed_10m, "trip_id", "left")
        # DEFECT 3 - weather joined to the trip's OWN hour; the file lands after it.
        .join(weather.select(F.col("city").alias("w_city"), "hour_ts",
                             F.col("condition").alias("weather_condition")),
              (F.col("city") == F.col("w_city")) &
              (F.date_trunc("hour", F.col("pickup_ts")) == F.col("hour_ts")), "left")
        # DEFECT 4 - distance_km is the METERED distance, written at dropoff_ts.
        # DEFECT 5 - the label is present and is materialised downstream.
        .select("trip_id", "pickup_zone_id", "dropoff_zone_id",
                "hour_of_day", "day_of_week",
                "rolling_zone_demand_15m", "rolling_avg_speed_10m",
                "driver_recent_trip_count", "weather_condition",
                "distance_km", "historical_route_duration", "feature_ts",
                F.col("duration_min").alias("label_actual_duration_min")))

    assert len(out.columns) == 13, out.columns
    out.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(OUT)
    print(f"[pa3-setup] eta_features: {out.count():,} rows, 13 columns -> {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
# MODEL CARD — masar-eta-duration  v3.1
**Owner:** ETA & Demand squad          **Status:** approved for production rollout
**Task:** predict `label_actual_duration_min` (trip duration, minutes)
**Training data:** `gold.eta_features`, 42,038 rows, 2026-06-01 .. 2026-06-30
**Split:** random 75 / 25
**Algorithm:** GradientBoostingRegressor (sklearn defaults, n_estimators=200)

## Offline performance
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| R2   | **0.941** |
| MAE  | **1.87 min** |
| RMSE | 2.94 min |

## Top features by gain
| Feature | Gain |
|---|---|
| distance_km               | 0.601 |
| historical_route_duration | 0.208 |
| rolling_zone_demand_15m   | 0.079 |
| rolling_avg_speed_10m     | 0.058 |
| driver_recent_trip_count  | 0.022 |

## Serving
Online features are read from Redis `masar:features:zone:{zone_id}`, refreshed by
the nightly gold DAG. `ONLINE_COLUMNS = [rolling_zone_demand_15m,
rolling_avg_speed_10m, historical_route_duration, weather_condition,
driver_recent_trip_count, label_actual_duration_min]`.

## Known limitations
None material. Model is stable across cities; no drift observed in 30 days.

Two further defects are hidden in the card, not the table, and the marking scheme rewards finding them: the random 75/25 split (which leaks across time on a temporally ordered table) and the label in ONLINE_COLUMNS (which materialises the answer into the online store).
